title:	Duplicate merge assistant: merge two members in place from the quality report
state:	OPEN
author:	maxi-smidt (Maximilian Smidt)
labels:	enhancement
comments:	0
assignees:	
projects:	
milestone:	
issue-type:	
parent:	
sub-issues:	
sub-issues-completed:	
blocked-by:	
blocking:	
number:	729
--
## Context

Two finished subsystems aren't connected yet:

- the quality report flags `duplicate_candidate` pairs ([`quality_checks.py`](backend/app/services/quality_checks.py)), but offers only *dismiss* — no way to act on a real duplicate;
- [`merge.py`](backend/app/services/merge.py) already has `compute_merge_preview` and per-pair, per-field conflict `resolutions` (#166) — but only for **tree-level** merges that produce a brand-new tree.

Merging two members *within* a tree currently means manually re-wiring relations and links, then deleting one row. Duplicates are the most persistent data-quality problem in genealogy.

## Goal

A guided in-place merge of two members of the same tree, launched from a `duplicate_candidate` finding in the quality-report view (and optionally from member selection in the tree).

## Scope

- **Backend**: `POST /trees/{tree_id}/members/merge` taking `(keep_id, remove_id, field resolutions)`:
  - preview endpoint first (reuse/extract the field-conflict logic from `compute_merge_preview` rather than forking it);
  - union relations (dedup, drop self-relations), re-point parent references (`maternalParent`/`paternalParent`) of children, transfer event/story/gallery/document/disease links, keep the chosen photo, combine notes;
  - guard rails: both members in the same tree, refuse merging a member with itself, refuse when it would create a relationship cycle (reuse the cycle check from quality checks);
  - `record_activity` with a rich payload — ideally the full pre-image, aligning with #572 so merges become reversible later.
- **Frontend**: "Merge…" action on `duplicate_candidate` findings in `QualityReportView` → dialog with side-by-side field comparison and per-field pick (shape borrowed from the tree-merge resolution UI), preview of what will be transferred, confirm.
- Entry point lives behind the existing `quality_report` flag; the endpoint itself is core member CRUD (not separately flagged).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Preview shows field conflicts and what will be transferred before anything is written
- [ ] After merge: all relations/links/content of the removed member are attached to the kept member, no dangling references, layout recomputes cleanly
- [ ] Cycle/self-merge guards with clear errors
- [ ] Activity log entry with enough detail to audit the merge
- [ ] Backend tests for relation re-pointing, link transfer, and guard rails
- [ ] i18n keys in every locale

268	def _wire_bridge(source: Member, counterpart: Member) -> None:
269	    """Point two member rows at each other as a bridge person pair.
270	
271	    Shared by every flow that establishes a tree-in-tree link (create-linked-
272	    subtree, extract-subtree, and the link-existing-tree endpoint) so the
273	    bidirectional wiring stays in one place.
274	    """
275	    source.linked_tree_id = counterpart.tree_id
276	    source.linked_member_id = counterpart.id
277	    counterpart.linked_tree_id = source.tree_id
278	    counterpart.linked_member_id = source.id

281	def apply_field_choices(
282	    clone: Member,
283	    ma: Member,
284	    mb: Member,
285	    fields: dict[str, str],
286	) -> None:
287	    """Apply per-field resolution choices to a merged clone.
288	
289	    ``clone`` was already built from ``ma`` (source A); we apply overrides here.
290	    ``fields`` maps field_name → "a" | "b" | "combine".
291	    """
292	    text_fields = {"additional_data", "places_lived"}
293	    for field, choice in fields.items():
294	        if field not in CONFLICT_FIELDS:
295	            continue
296	        va = getattr(ma, field, None)
297	        vb = getattr(mb, field, None)
298	        if choice == "a":
299	            setattr(clone, field, va)
300	        elif choice == "b":
301	            setattr(clone, field, vb)
302	        elif choice == "combine" and field in text_fields:
303	            separator = "\n\n" if field == "additional_data" else ", "
304	            parts = [p for p in [va, vb] if not _empty(p)]
305	            # Deduplicate while preserving order
306	            seen: list[str] = []
307	            for p in parts:
308	                if p not in seen:
309	                    seen.append(p)
310	            setattr(clone, field, separator.join(seen) if seen else None)
311	
312	
313	def reconcile_bridge_fields(
314	    member: Member,
315	    counterpart: Member,
316	    choices: dict[str, str] | None = None,
317	) -> None:
318	    """Reconcile the conflicting fields of a freshly-wired bridge pair.
319	
320	    Used by the link-existing-tree flow (mode="existing") right after
321	    ``_wire_bridge``: the two rows represent the same human, so once linked
322	    their conflicting fields (dates, places, images, notes, ...) should agree
323	    on both sides, not just drift until a later edit or bridge-sync.
324	
325	    For each field in ``CONFLICT_FIELDS`` an explicit choice ("a" | "b" |
326	    "combine", a = ``member``, b = ``counterpart``) from ``choices`` is
327	    applied when given; otherwise the fields are unioned (whichever side is
328	    non-empty wins, preferring ``member`` when both are set) via the same
329	    a/b/combine semantics as ``apply_field_choices``. ``image_data`` is copied
330	    into the destination tree's media store, mirroring
331	    ``bridge.copy_bridge_fields``.
332	
333	    ``choices`` keys may be camelCase (as sent by the frontend, matching its
334	    ``RESOLVABLE_FIELDS``) or snake_case; both are normalised to the
335	    ``Member`` attribute name.
336	    """
337	    choices = choices or {}
338	    normalised_choices = {_to_snake_case(k): v for k, v in choices.items()}
339	    resolved: dict[str, str] = {
340	        k: v for k, v in normalised_choices.items() if k in CONFLICT_FIELDS
341	    }
342	    for field in CONFLICT_FIELDS:
343	        if field in resolved:
344	            continue
345	        va = getattr(member, field, None)
346	        vb = getattr(counterpart, field, None)
347	        # Union default: prefer whichever side is non-empty; when both are
348	        # set (a genuine conflict with no explicit choice) keep A's value.
349	        resolved[field] = "a" if not _empty(va) or _empty(vb) else "b"
350	
351	    # Snapshot pre-reconciliation values so both a→b and b→a copies read the
352	    # same source data even though `member` is mutated first below.
353	    orig_member = {f: getattr(member, f, None) for f in CONFLICT_FIELDS}
354	    orig_counterpart = {f: getattr(counterpart, f, None) for f in CONFLICT_FIELDS}
355	
356	    for field, choice in resolved.items():
357	        if choice == "a":
358	            value = orig_member[field]
359	        elif choice == "b":
360	            value = orig_counterpart[field]
361	        else:  # combine
362	            if field in {"additional_data", "places_lived"}:
363	                separator = "\n\n" if field == "additional_data" else ", "
364	                parts = [
365	                    p for p in [orig_member[field], orig_counterpart[field]]
366	                    if not _empty(p)
367	                ]
368	                seen: list[str] = []
369	                for p in parts:
370	                    if p not in seen:
371	                        seen.append(p)
372	                value = separator.join(seen) if seen else None
373	            else:
374	                # Combine doesn't apply to non-text fields; fall back to A.
375	                value = orig_member[field]
376	
377	        if field == "image_data":
378	            member.image_data = (
379	                value if value == orig_member["image_data"]
380	                else copy_media_to_tree(value, member.tree_id)
381	            )
382	            counterpart.image_data = (
383	                value if value == orig_counterpart["image_data"]
384	                else copy_media_to_tree(value, counterpart.tree_id)
385	            )
386	        else:
387	            setattr(member, field, value)
388	            setattr(counterpart, field, value)
389

395	def _build_resolution_index(
396	    resolutions: list[MergeResolution] | None,
397	) -> dict[frozenset, MergeResolution]:
398	    """Map {frozenset({id_a, id_b})} → resolution for O(1) lookup."""
399	    if not resolutions:
400	        return {}
401	    return {frozenset({r.member_a_id, r.member_b_id}): r for r in resolutions}

407	
408	def merge_trees(
409	    db: Session,
410	    user: User,
411	    name: str,
412	    source_a_id: str,
413	    source_b_id: str | None,
414	    resolutions: list[MergeResolution] | None = None,
415	    progress_cb: ProgressCallback | None = None,
416	) -> Tree:
417	    def _progress(pct: int) -> None:
418	        if progress_cb is not None:
419	            progress_cb(pct)
420	
421	    tree_a = _require_readable(db, user, source_a_id)
422	    tree_b = _require_readable(db, user, source_b_id) if source_b_id else None
423	    sources = [t for t in (tree_a, tree_b) if t is not None]
424	
425	    res_index = _build_resolution_index(resolutions)
426	
427	    new_tree = Tree(
428	        id=str(uuid4()),
429	        name=name,
430	        owner_id=user.id,
431	        created_at=utcnow_iso(),
432	        last_opened=utcnow_iso(),
433	    )
434	    db.add(new_tree)
435	    db.flush()
436	    _progress(10)
437	
438	    # --- Members (with de-duplication across both sources) -----------------
439	    # member_map: source member id → new tree member id
440	    member_map: dict[str, str] = {}
441	    # dedup: exact-match key → clone Member object (so we can apply field merges)
442	    dedup: dict[tuple, Member] = {}
443	    # name-key index for possible-candidate detection
444	    name_index: dict[tuple, tuple[Member, str]] = {}  # name_key → (clone, original_a_id)
445	
446	    # Collect all members from source A first
447	    members_a = list(db.scalars(select(Member).where(Member.tree_id == tree_a.id)))
448	    members_b = (
449	        list(db.scalars(select(Member).where(Member.tree_id == tree_b.id)))
450	        if tree_b
451	        else []
452	    )
453	
454	    # ---- Pass 1: clone all source-A members ----
455	    for ma in members_a:
456	        new_id = str(uuid4())
457	        member_map[ma.id] = new_id
458	        clone = _clone_member(ma, new_tree.id, new_id)
459	        db.add(clone)
460	        dedup[member_key(ma)] = clone
461	        name_index[member_name_key(ma)] = (clone, ma.id)
462	
463	    # ---- Pass 2: process source-B members ----
464	    for mb in members_b:
465	        exact_key = member_key(mb)
466	        name_key = member_name_key(mb)
467	
468	        # --- Check resolution for this pair (if any) ---
469	        # We need to find the matching source-A member to look up the resolution.
470	        matched_a_clone: Member | None = dedup.get(exact_key)
471	        matched_a_id: str | None = None
472	        match_type: str | None = None
473	
474	        if matched_a_clone is not None:
475	            # Exact match found
476	            # Find the original A member id from the member_map (reverse lookup)
477	            for orig_id, new_id in member_map.items():
478	                if new_id == matched_a_clone.id:
479	                    matched_a_id = orig_id
480	                    break
481	            match_type = "exact"
482	        elif name_key in name_index:
483	            # Possible candidate (name+gender match, dates differ)
484	            matched_a_clone, matched_a_id = name_index[name_key]
485	            match_type = "possible"
486	
487	        if matched_a_id is not None and matched_a_clone is not None:
488	            res_key = frozenset({matched_a_id, mb.id})
489	            resolution = res_index.get(res_key)
490	
491	            if match_type == "exact":
492	                # Default behaviour: merge (unless keep_both resolution)
493	                action = resolution.action if resolution else "merge"
494	            else:
495	                # Possible candidate: default keep_both (unless merge resolution)
496	                action = resolution.action if resolution else "keep_both"
497	
498	            if action == "keep_both":
499	                # Clone B as a separate member
500	                new_id = str(uuid4())
501	                member_map[mb.id] = new_id
502	                clone_b = _clone_member(mb, new_tree.id, new_id)
503	                db.add(clone_b)
504	            else:
505	                # Merge: B maps to A's clone; apply field choices if given
506	                member_map[mb.id] = matched_a_clone.id
507	                if resolution and resolution.fields:
508	                    # Find the original A member for field comparison
509	                    orig_ma = next(
510	                        (m for m in members_a if m.id == matched_a_id), None
511	                    )
512	                    if orig_ma is not None:
513	                        apply_field_choices(
514	                            matched_a_clone, orig_ma, mb, resolution.fields
515	                        )
516	                else:
517	                    # Legacy behaviour: combine additional_data
518	                    if (
519	                        mb.additional_data
520	                        and mb.additional_data != matched_a_clone.additional_data
521	                    ):
522	                        matched_a_clone.additional_data = (
523	                            f"{matched_a_clone.additional_data}\n\n{mb.additional_data}"
524	                            if matched_a_clone.additional_data
525	                            else mb.additional_data
526	                        )
527	        else:
528	            # No match: always clone as new
529	            new_id = str(uuid4())
530	            member_map[mb.id] = new_id
531	            clone = _clone_member(mb, new_tree.id, new_id)
532	            db.add(clone)
533	
534	    # Members must exist before relations/diseases/links reference them.
535	    db.flush()
536	    _progress(50)
537	
538	    # --- Relations ---------------------------------------------------------
539	    seen_relations: set[tuple] = set()
540	    for t in sources:
541	        for r in db.scalars(select(Relation).where(Relation.tree_id == t.id)):
542	            f = member_map.get(r.from_member_id)
543	            to = member_map.get(r.to_member_id)
544	            if not f or not to:
545	                continue
546	            key = (f, to, r.relation_type)
547	            if key not in seen_relations:
548	                seen_relations.add(key)
549	                db.add(
550	                    Relation(
551	                        tree_id=new_tree.id,
552	                        from_member_id=f,
553	                        to_member_id=to,
554	                        relation_type=r.relation_type,
555	                    )
556	                )

559	    seen_diseases: set[tuple] = set()
560	    for t in sources:

562	            mid = member_map.get(d.member_id)

576	                    inheritance_pattern=d.inheritance_pattern,
577	                    diagnosis_date=d.diagnosis_date,
578	                    notes=d.notes,
579	                )
580	            )
581

583	    # seen_tasks maps the dedup key to the surviving merged task id, and

586	    seen_tasks: dict[tuple, str] = {}

612	            db.add(

618	                    done=task.done,
619	                    created_at=task.created_at,

621	                )

626	    _progress(60)
627	
628	    # --- Gallery images + links --------------------------------------------
629	    image_map: dict[str, str] = {}

824	    seen_event_doc_links: set[tuple] = set()

"""Server-side tree merge.

Combines one or two source trees into a brand-new tree owned by the requesting
user. Members are de-duplicated by (first name, last name, gender, birth, death)
— matching the old client-side merge — and notes from duplicates are combined.
All ids are regenerated (ids are globally unique here), relations/links are
remapped, and member photos / gallery media are copied into the new tree.

New in #166: ``compute_merge_preview`` for a preview endpoint, and optional
per-pair ``resolutions`` that let callers override merge vs keep_both and
choose field values on a conflict.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
from uuid import uuid4

from fastapi import HTTPException
from sqlalchemy import select
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from app.api.deps import role_for
from app.db.base import utcnow_iso
from app.models import (
    Document,
    DocumentFile,
    DocumentMemberLink,
    Event,
    EventDocumentLink,
    EventMemberLink,
    GalleryImage,
    GalleryMemberLink,
    GalleryUnknownFace,
    Member,
    MemberDisease,
    MemberTask,
    MemberTaskLink,
    Relation,
    Story,
    StoryDocumentLink,
    StoryMemberLink,
    Tree,
    User,
)
from app.schemas.family import MemberOut
from app.schemas.merge import DuplicatePair, MergeResolution, TreeMergePreview
from app.services.activity import record_activity
from app.services.event_bus import publish_tree_event
from app.services.job_service import ProgressCallback
from app.services.storage import copy_media_to_tree

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    pass


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Normalisation helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _norm(value: str | None) -> str:
    return (value or "").strip().lower()


def _empty(value: str | None) -> bool:
    """True when the value should be treated as absent (None or blank)."""
    return not (value or "").strip()


_CAMEL_BOUNDARY = re.compile(r"(?<!^)(?=[A-Z])")


def _to_snake_case(name: str) -> str:
    """Convert a camelCase field name (as the frontend sends field_choices /
    merge resolution keys) to the snake_case attribute name used on
    ``Member``. Already-snake_case input passes through unchanged."""
    return _CAMEL_BOUNDARY.sub("_", name).lower()


def member_key(m: Member) -> tuple:
    """Exact-duplicate key: name + gender + both dates (all normalised)."""
    return (
        _norm(m.first_name), _norm(m.last_name),
        m.gender, m.date_of_birth, m.date_of_death,
    )


def member_name_key(m: Member) -> tuple:
    """Name + gender only — used for possible-candidate detection."""
    return (_norm(m.first_name), _norm(m.last_name), m.gender)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Auth guard
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _require_readable(db: Session, user: User, tree_id: str) -> Tree:
    tree = db.get(Tree, tree_id)
    if tree is None or role_for(db, tree, user) is None:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Source tree not found")
    return tree


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Conflict detection
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

CONFLICT_FIELDS: list[str] = [
    "middle_names",
    "baptismal_name",
    "maiden_name",
    "birthplace",
    "hometown",
    "cemetery",
    "places_lived",
    "additional_data",
    "image_data",
    "date_of_birth",
    "date_of_death",
]


def compute_conflicts(a: Member, b: Member) -> list[str]:
    """Return field names where the two members differ in a meaningful way."""
    conflicts: list[str] = []
    for field in CONFLICT_FIELDS:
        va = getattr(a, field, None)
        vb = getattr(b, field, None)
        if field == "image_data":
            # Report conflict only when both are set and differ
            if not _empty(va) and not _empty(vb) and va != vb:
                conflicts.append(field)
        else:
            # Treat None and "" as equal-empty
            if _empty(va) and _empty(vb):
                continue
            if (va or "") != (vb or ""):
                conflicts.append(field)
    return conflicts


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Preview computation
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def compute_merge_preview(
    db: Session,
    user: User,
    source_a_id: str,
    source_b_id: str | None,
) -> TreeMergePreview:
    """Compute a merge preview without touching the database."""
    tree_a = _require_readable(db, user, source_a_id)
    tree_b = _require_readable(db, user, source_b_id) if source_b_id else None

    members_a: list[Member] = list(
        db.scalars(select(Member).where(Member.tree_id == tree_a.id))
    )
    members_b: list[Member] = (
        list(db.scalars(select(Member).where(Member.tree_id == tree_b.id)))
        if tree_b
        else []
    )

    total_members = len(members_a) + len(members_b)

    if not members_b:
        # Single-source copy: no duplicates possible
        return TreeMergePreview(
            total_members=total_members,
            merged_count=total_members,
            duplicates=[],
        )

    # Index source-A members by exact key and by name key
    exact_by_key: dict[tuple, Member] = {}
    name_by_key: dict[tuple, Member] = {}
    for m in members_a:
        exact_by_key[member_key(m)] = m
        name_by_key[member_name_key(m)] = m

    duplicates: list[DuplicatePair] = []
    exact_matched_b_ids: set[str] = set()
    possible_matched_b_ids: set[str] = set()

    # First pass: exact duplicates
    for mb in members_b:
        exact_key = member_key(mb)
        if exact_key in exact_by_key:
            ma = exact_by_key[exact_key]
            conflicts = compute_conflicts(ma, mb)
            duplicates.append(
                DuplicatePair(
                    member_a=MemberOut.model_validate(ma),
                    member_b=MemberOut.model_validate(mb),
                    match="exact",
                    conflicts=conflicts,
                    default_action="merge",
                )
            )
            exact_matched_b_ids.add(mb.id)

    # Second pass: possible candidates (name+gender match, but dates differ)
    for mb in members_b:
        if mb.id in exact_matched_b_ids:
            continue
        name_key = member_name_key(mb)
        if name_key in name_by_key:
            ma = name_by_key[name_key]
            # Sanity check: must not be an exact match (already handled above)
            if member_key(ma) == member_key(mb):
                continue
            conflicts = compute_conflicts(ma, mb)
            duplicates.append(
                DuplicatePair(
                    member_a=MemberOut.model_validate(ma),
                    member_b=MemberOut.model_validate(mb),
                    match="possible",
                    conflicts=conflicts,
                    default_action="keep_both",
                )
            )
            possible_matched_b_ids.add(mb.id)

    # merged_count = how many rows the result tree would have (under defaults)
    # Exact dupes → 1 row; possible → 2 rows (default keep_both)
    merged_count = total_members - len(exact_matched_b_ids)

    return TreeMergePreview(
        total_members=total_members,
        merged_count=merged_count,
        duplicates=duplicates,
    )


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Clone helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _clone_member(m: Member, new_tree_id: str, new_id: str) -> Member:
    return Member(
        id=new_id,
        tree_id=new_tree_id,
        gender=m.gender,
        academic_title=m.academic_title,
        deceased=m.deceased,
        adopted=m.adopted,
        first_name=m.first_name,
        middle_names=m.middle_names,
        baptismal_name=m.baptismal_name,
        last_name=m.last_name,
        maiden_name=m.maiden_name,
        image_data=copy_media_to_tree(m.image_data, new_tree_id),
        date_of_birth=m.date_of_birth,
        date_of_death=m.date_of_death,
        additional_data=m.additional_data,
        is_collapsed=m.is_collapsed,
        position_x=m.position_x,
        position_y=m.position_y,
        birthplace=m.birthplace,
        hometown=m.hometown,
        cemetery=m.cemetery,
        places_lived=m.places_lived,
    )


def _wire_bridge(source: Member, counterpart: Member) -> None:
    """Point two member rows at each other as a bridge person pair.

    Shared by every flow that establishes a tree-in-tree link (create-linked-
    subtree, extract-subtree, and the link-existing-tree endpoint) so the
    bidirectional wiring stays in one place.
    """
    source.linked_tree_id = counterpart.tree_id
    source.linked_member_id = counterpart.id
    counterpart.linked_tree_id = source.tree_id
    counterpart.linked_member_id = source.id


def apply_field_choices(
    clone: Member,
    ma: Member,
    mb: Member,
    fields: dict[str, str],
) -> None:
    """Apply per-field resolution choices to a merged clone.

    ``clone`` was already built from ``ma`` (source A); we apply overrides here.
    ``fields`` maps field_name → "a" | "b" | "combine".
    """
    text_fields = {"additional_data", "places_lived"}
    for field, choice in fields.items():
        if field not in CONFLICT_FIELDS:
            continue
        va = getattr(ma, field, None)
        vb = getattr(mb, field, None)
        if choice == "a":
            setattr(clone, field, va)
        elif choice == "b":
            setattr(clone, field, vb)
        elif choice == "combine" and field in text_fields:
            separator = "\n\n" if field == "additional_data" else ", "
            parts = [p for p in [va, vb] if not _empty(p)]
            # Deduplicate while preserving order
            seen: list[str] = []
            for p in parts:
                if p not in seen:
                    seen.append(p)
            setattr(clone, field, separator.join(seen) if seen else None)


def reconcile_bridge_fields(
    member: Member,
    counterpart: Member,
    choices: dict[str, str] | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Reconcile the conflicting fields of a freshly-wired bridge pair.

    Used by the link-existing-tree flow (mode="existing") right after
    ``_wire_bridge``: the two rows represent the same human, so once linked
    their conflicting fields (dates, places, images, notes, ...) should agree
    on both sides, not just drift until a later edit or bridge-sync.

    For each field in ``CONFLICT_FIELDS`` an explicit choice ("a" | "b" |
    "combine", a = ``member``, b = ``counterpart``) from ``choices`` is
    applied when given; otherwise the fields are unioned (whichever side is
    non-empty wins, preferring ``member`` when both are set) via the same
    a/b/combine semantics as ``apply_field_choices``. ``image_data`` is copied
    into the destination tree's media store, mirroring
    ``bridge.copy_bridge_fields``.

    ``choices`` keys may be camelCase (as sent by the frontend, matching its
    ``RESOLVABLE_FIELDS``) or snake_case; both are normalised to the
    ``Member`` attribute name.
    """
    choices = choices or {}
    normalised_choices = {_to_snake_case(k): v for k, v in choices.items()}
    resolved: dict[str, str] = {
        k: v for k, v in normalised_choices.items() if k in CONFLICT_FIELDS
    }
    for field in CONFLICT_FIELDS:
        if field in resolved:
            continue
        va = getattr(member, field, None)
        vb = getattr(counterpart, field, None)
        # Union default: prefer whichever side is non-empty; when both are
        # set (a genuine conflict with no explicit choice) keep A's value.
        resolved[field] = "a" if not _empty(va) or _empty(vb) else "b"

    # Snapshot pre-reconciliation values so both a→b and b→a copies read the
    # same source data even though `member` is mutated first below.
    orig_member = {f: getattr(member, f, None) for f in CONFLICT_FIELDS}
    orig_counterpart = {f: getattr(counterpart, f, None) for f in CONFLICT_FIELDS}

    for field, choice in resolved.items():
        if choice == "a":
            value = orig_member[field]
        elif choice == "b":
            value = orig_counterpart[field]
        else:  # combine
            if field in {"additional_data", "places_lived"}:
                separator = "\n\n" if field == "additional_data" else ", "
                parts = [
                    p for p in [orig_member[field], orig_counterpart[field]]
                    if not _empty(p)
                ]
                seen: list[str] = []
                for p in parts:
                    if p not in seen:
                        seen.append(p)
                value = separator.join(seen) if seen else None
            else:
                # Combine doesn't apply to non-text fields; fall back to A.
                value = orig_member[field]

        if field == "image_data":
            member.image_data = (
                value if value == orig_member["image_data"]
                else copy_media_to_tree(value, member.tree_id)
            )
            counterpart.image_data = (
                value if value == orig_counterpart["image_data"]
                else copy_media_to_tree(value, counterpart.tree_id)
            )
        else:
            setattr(member, field, value)
            setattr(counterpart, field, value)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Resolution index helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _build_resolution_index(
    resolutions: list[MergeResolution] | None,
) -> dict[frozenset, MergeResolution]:
    """Map {frozenset({id_a, id_b})} → resolution for O(1) lookup."""
    if not resolutions:
        return {}
    return {frozenset({r.member_a_id, r.member_b_id}): r for r in resolutions}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Main merge entry point
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def merge_trees(
    db: Session,
    user: User,
    name: str,
    source_a_id: str,
    source_b_id: str | None,
    resolutions: list[MergeResolution] | None = None,
    progress_cb: ProgressCallback | None = None,
) -> Tree:
    def _progress(pct: int) -> None:
        if progress_cb is not None:
            progress_cb(pct)

    tree_a = _require_readable(db, user, source_a_id)
    tree_b = _require_readable(db, user, source_b_id) if source_b_id else None
    sources = [t for t in (tree_a, tree_b) if t is not None]

    res_index = _build_resolution_index(resolutions)

    new_tree = Tree(
        id=str(uuid4()),
        name=name,
        owner_id=user.id,
        created_at=utcnow_iso(),
        last_opened=utcnow_iso(),
    )
    db.add(new_tree)
    db.flush()
    _progress(10)

    # --- Members (with de-duplication across both sources) -----------------
    # member_map: source member id → new tree member id
    member_map: dict[str, str] = {}
    # dedup: exact-match key → clone Member object (so we can apply field merges)
    dedup: dict[tuple, Member] = {}
    # name-key index for possible-candidate detection
    name_index: dict[tuple, tuple[Member, str]] = {}  # name_key → (clone, original_a_id)

    # Collect all members from source A first
    members_a = list(db.scalars(select(Member).where(Member.tree_id == tree_a.id)))
    members_b = (
        list(db.scalars(select(Member).where(Member.tree_id == tree_b.id)))
        if tree_b
        else []
    )

    # ---- Pass 1: clone all source-A members ----
    for ma in members_a:
        new_id = str(uuid4())
        member_map[ma.id] = new_id
        clone = _clone_member(ma, new_tree.id, new_id)
        db.add(clone)
        dedup[member_key(ma)] = clone
        name_index[member_name_key(ma)] = (clone, ma.id)

    # ---- Pass 2: process source-B members ----
    for mb in members_b:
        exact_key = member_key(mb)
        name_key = member_name_key(mb)

        # --- Check resolution for this pair (if any) ---
        # We need to find the matching source-A member to look up the resolution.
        matched_a_clone: Member | None = dedup.get(exact_key)
        matched_a_id: str | None = None
        match_type: str | None = None

        if matched_a_clone is not None:
            # Exact match found
            # Find the original A member id from the member_map (reverse lookup)
            for orig_id, new_id in member_map.items():
                if new_id == matched_a_clone.id:
                    matched_a_id = orig_id
                    break
            match_type = "exact"
        elif name_key in name_index:
            # Possible candidate (name+gender match, dates differ)
            matched_a_clone, matched_a_id = name_index[name_key]
            match_type = "possible"

        if matched_a_id is not None and matched_a_clone is not None:
            res_key = frozenset({matched_a_id, mb.id})
            resolution = res_index.get(res_key)

            if match_type == "exact":
                # Default behaviour: merge (unless keep_both resolution)
                action = resolution.action if resolution else "merge"
            else:
                # Possible candidate: default keep_both (unless merge resolution)
                action = resolution.action if resolution else "keep_both"

            if action == "keep_both":
                # Clone B as a separate member
                new_id = str(uuid4())
                member_map[mb.id] = new_id
                clone_b = _clone_member(mb, new_tree.id, new_id)
                db.add(clone_b)
            else:
                # Merge: B maps to A's clone; apply field choices if given
                member_map[mb.id] = matched_a_clone.id
                if resolution and resolution.fields:
                    # Find the original A member for field comparison
                    orig_ma = next(
                        (m for m in members_a if m.id == matched_a_id), None
                    )
                    if orig_ma is not None:
                        apply_field_choices(
                            matched_a_clone, orig_ma, mb, resolution.fields
                        )
                else:
                    # Legacy behaviour: combine additional_data
                    if (
                        mb.additional_data
                        and mb.additional_data != matched_a_clone.additional_data
                    ):
                        matched_a_clone.additional_data = (
                            f"{matched_a_clone.additional_data}\n\n{mb.additional_data}"
                            if matched_a_clone.additional_data
                            else mb.additional_data
                        )
        else:
            # No match: always clone as new
            new_id = str(uuid4())
            member_map[mb.id] = new_id
            clone = _clone_member(mb, new_tree.id, new_id)
            db.add(clone)

    # Members must exist before relations/diseases/links reference them.
    db.flush()
    _progress(50)

    # --- Relations ---------------------------------------------------------
    seen_relations: set[tuple] = set()
    for t in sources:
        for r in db.scalars(select(Relation).where(Relation.tree_id == t.id)):
            f = member_map.get(r.from_member_id)
            to = member_map.get(r.to_member_id)
            if not f or not to:
                continue
            key = (f, to, r.relation_type)
            if key not in seen_relations:
                seen_relations.add(key)
                db.add(
                    Relation(
                        tree_id=new_tree.id,
                        from_member_id=f,
                        to_member_id=to,
                        relation_type=r.relation_type,
                    )
                )

    # --- Diseases (deduped by member + name) -------------------------------
    seen_diseases: set[tuple] = set()
    for t in sources:
        for d in db.scalars(select(MemberDisease).where(MemberDisease.tree_id == t.id)):
            mid = member_map.get(d.member_id)
            if mid is None:
                continue
            key = (mid, _norm(d.name))
            if key in seen_diseases:
                continue
            seen_diseases.add(key)
            db.add(
                MemberDisease(
                    id=str(uuid4()),
                    tree_id=new_tree.id,
                    member_id=mid,
                    name=d.name,
                    carrier_status=d.carrier_status,
                    inheritance_pattern=d.inheritance_pattern,
                    diagnosis_date=d.diagnosis_date,
                    notes=d.notes,
                )
            )

    # --- Research tasks (deduped by linked-member set + title) --------------
    # seen_tasks maps the dedup key to the surviving merged task id, and
    # task_id_map maps every source task id to it, so rows referencing tasks
    # (gallery unknown faces below) can follow their task into the merge.
    seen_tasks: dict[tuple, str] = {}
    task_id_map: dict[str, str] = {}
    for t in sources:
        source_links: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
        link_rows = db.execute(
            select(MemberTaskLink)
            .join(MemberTask, MemberTask.id == MemberTaskLink.task_id)
            .where(MemberTask.tree_id == t.id)
        ).scalars()
        for link in link_rows:
            source_links.setdefault(link.task_id, []).append(link.member_id)
        for task in db.scalars(select(MemberTask).where(MemberTask.tree_id == t.id)):
            mapped_members = sorted(
                {
                    member_map[mid]
                    for mid in source_links.get(task.id, [])
                    if mid in member_map
                }
            )
            key = (frozenset(mapped_members), _norm(task.title))
            if key in seen_tasks:
                task_id_map[task.id] = seen_tasks[key]
                continue
            new_task_id = str(uuid4())
            seen_tasks[key] = new_task_id
            task_id_map[task.id] = new_task_id
            db.add(
                MemberTask(
                    id=new_task_id,
                    tree_id=new_tree.id,
                    title=task.title,
                    notes=task.notes,
                    done=task.done,
                    created_at=task.created_at,
                    done_at=task.done_at,
                )
            )
            for mid in mapped_members:
                db.add(MemberTaskLink(task_id=new_task_id, member_id=mid))

    _progress(60)

    # --- Gallery images + links --------------------------------------------
    image_map: dict[str, str] = {}
    for t in sources:
        for img in db.scalars(select(GalleryImage).where(GalleryImage.tree_id == t.id)):
            new_id = str(uuid4())
            image_map[img.id] = new_id
            db.add(
                GalleryImage(
                    id=new_id,
                    tree_id=new_tree.id,
                    image_data=copy_media_to_tree(img.image_data, new_tree.id),
                    title=img.title,
                    description=img.description,
                    created_at=img.created_at,
                    uploaded_at=img.uploaded_at,
                )
            )
    db.flush()  # gallery images before their links
    seen_gallery_links: set[tuple] = set()
    for t in sources:
        links = db.scalars(
            select(GalleryMemberLink)
            .join(GalleryImage, GalleryImage.id == GalleryMemberLink.gallery_image_id)
            .where(GalleryImage.tree_id == t.id)
        )
        for link in links:
            gi = image_map.get(link.gallery_image_id)
            mid = member_map.get(link.member_id)
            if gi and mid and (gi, mid) not in seen_gallery_links:
                seen_gallery_links.add((gi, mid))
                db.add(
                    GalleryMemberLink(
                        gallery_image_id=gi,
                        member_id=mid,
                        x=link.x,
                        y=link.y,
                        w=link.w,
                        h=link.h,
                    )
                )

    # --- Gallery unknown-face tags ------------------------------------------
    # Regions carry over with their image, and ``task_id`` follows the task
    # into the merge via task_id_map (falling back to null if the task was
    # somehow not copied), so resolving/deleting the face after the merge
    # still closes the right task.
    for t in sources:
        faces = db.scalars(
            select(GalleryUnknownFace)
            .join(GalleryImage, GalleryImage.id == GalleryUnknownFace.gallery_image_id)
            .where(GalleryImage.tree_id == t.id)
        )
        for face in faces:
            gi = image_map.get(face.gallery_image_id)
            if gi:
                db.add(
                    GalleryUnknownFace(
                        id=str(uuid4()),
                        gallery_image_id=gi,
                        x=face.x,
                        y=face.y,
                        w=face.w,
                        h=face.h,
                        task_id=(
                            task_id_map.get(face.task_id) if face.task_id else None
                        ),
                        created_at=face.created_at,
                    )
                )

    _progress(70)

    # --- Events + links ----------------------------------------------------
    event_map: dict[str, str] = {}
    for t in sources:
        for e in db.scalars(select(Event).where(Event.tree_id == t.id)):
            new_id = str(uuid4())
            event_map[e.id] = new_id
            db.add(
                Event(
                    id=new_id,
                    tree_id=new_tree.id,
                    event_type=e.event_type,
                    date=e.date,
                    location=e.location,
                    description=e.description,
                    created_at=e.created_at,
                )
            )
    db.flush()  # events before their links
    seen_event_links: set[tuple] = set()
    for t in sources:
        links = db.scalars(
            select(EventMemberLink)
            .join(Event, Event.id == EventMemberLink.event_id)
            .where(Event.tree_id == t.id)
        )
        for link in links:
            ev = event_map.get(link.event_id)
            mid = member_map.get(link.member_id)
            if ev and mid and (ev, mid) not in seen_event_links:
                seen_event_links.add((ev, mid))
                db.add(EventMemberLink(event_id=ev, member_id=mid))

    _progress(80)

    # --- Stories + links ---------------------------------------------------
    story_map: dict[str, str] = {}
    for t in sources:
        for s in db.scalars(select(Story).where(Story.tree_id == t.id)):
            new_id = str(uuid4())
            story_map[s.id] = new_id
            db.add(
                Story(
                    id=new_id,
                    tree_id=new_tree.id,
                    title=s.title,
                    content=s.content,
                    created_at=s.created_at,
                    updated_at=s.updated_at,
                )
            )
    db.flush()  # stories before their links
    seen_story_links: set[tuple] = set()
    for t in sources:
        links = db.scalars(
            select(StoryMemberLink)
            .join(Story, Story.id == StoryMemberLink.story_id)
            .where(Story.tree_id == t.id)
        )
        for link in links:
            st = story_map.get(link.story_id)
            mid = member_map.get(link.member_id)
            if st and mid and (st, mid) not in seen_story_links:
                seen_story_links.add((st, mid))
                db.add(StoryMemberLink(story_id=st, member_id=mid))

    # --- Documents + files + links -----------------------------------------
    # Documents are reusable, tree-scoped content. Copy each source tree's
    # documents (with their files) into the new tree and repoint the merged
    # member/event/story links to the copies, so no link crosses a tree
    # boundary.
    document_map: dict[str, str] = {}
    for t in sources:
        for doc in db.scalars(select(Document).where(Document.tree_id == t.id)):
            new_id = str(uuid4())
            document_map[doc.id] = new_id
            db.add(
                Document(
                    id=new_id,
                    tree_id=new_tree.id,
                    title=doc.title,
                    document_date=doc.document_date,
                    description=doc.description,
                    created_at=doc.created_at,
                    updated_at=doc.updated_at,
                )
            )
    db.flush()  # documents before their files/links
    for t in sources:
        for f in db.scalars(
            select(DocumentFile)
            .join(Document, Document.id == DocumentFile.document_id)
            .where(Document.tree_id == t.id)
        ):
            new_doc_id = document_map.get(f.document_id)
            if new_doc_id is None:
                continue
            new_url = f.url
            if f.kind == "file":
                new_url = copy_media_to_tree(f.url, new_tree.id) or f.url
            db.add(
                DocumentFile(
                    id=str(uuid4()),
                    tree_id=new_tree.id,
                    document_id=new_doc_id,
                    kind=f.kind,
                    filename=f.filename,
                    url=new_url,
                    mime_type=f.mime_type,
                    size=f.size,
                    created_at=f.created_at,
                )
            )
    seen_doc_member_links: set[tuple] = set()
    for t in sources:
        for link in db.scalars(
            select(DocumentMemberLink)
            .join(Document, Document.id == DocumentMemberLink.document_id)
            .where(Document.tree_id == t.id)
        ):
            nd = document_map.get(link.document_id)
            mid = member_map.get(link.member_id)
            if nd and mid and (nd, mid) not in seen_doc_member_links:
                seen_doc_member_links.add((nd, mid))
                db.add(DocumentMemberLink(document_id=nd, member_id=mid))
    seen_event_doc_links: set[tuple] = set()
    for t in sources:
        for link in db.scalars(
            select(EventDocumentLink)
            .join(Document, Document.id == EventDocumentLink.document_id)
            .where(Document.tree_id == t.id)
        ):
            ev = event_map.get(link.event_id)
            nd = document_map.get(link.document_id)
            if ev and nd and (ev, nd) not in seen_event_doc_links:
                seen_event_doc_links.add((ev, nd))
                db.add(EventDocumentLink(event_id=ev, document_id=nd))
    seen_story_doc_links: set[tuple] = set()
    for t in sources:
        for link in db.scalars(
            select(StoryDocumentLink)
            .join(Document, Document.id == StoryDocumentLink.document_id)
            .where(Document.tree_id == t.id)
        ):
            st = story_map.get(link.story_id)
            nd = document_map.get(link.document_id)
            if st and nd and (st, nd) not in seen_story_doc_links:
                seen_story_doc_links.add((st, nd))
                db.add(StoryDocumentLink(story_id=st, document_id=nd))

    _progress(95)
    record_activity(
        db, tree_id=new_tree.id, actor=user, action="create",
        target_type="merge", target_id=new_tree.id, target_label=new_tree.name,
    )
    db.commit()
    db.refresh(new_tree)
    publish_tree_event(db, new_tree, "activity.entry_added", {"tree_id": new_tree.id})
    return new_tree

1	"""Data-quality checks for a family tree."""
2	
3	import hashlib
4	from collections import defaultdict
5	
6	from app.models.content import Event, EventMemberLink
7	from app.models.family import Member, Relation
8	
9	# Minimum/maximum plausible age of a parent at their child's birth.
10	_MIN_PARENT_AGE = 10
11	_MAX_PARENT_AGE = 100
12	
13	# A child can legitimately be born shortly after their *father's* death
14	# (a posthumous birth, up to ~9 months later). Dates here are year-only, so a
15	# one-year grace window is allowed for fathers and unknown-gender parents. A
16	# birth after the *mother's* death is not biologically possible, so mothers get
17	# no grace.
18	_POSTHUMOUS_BIRTH_GRACE_YEARS = 1
19	
20	# Event types that legitimately happen after a person's death and should not
21	# be flagged by the event-after-death check.
22	_POST_DEATH_EVENT_TYPES = frozenset({"burial"})
23	
24	
25	def _year(date_str: str | None) -> int | None:
26	    if not date_str:
27	        return None
28	    try:
29	        return int(date_str.split("-")[0])
30	    except (ValueError, IndexError):
31	        return None
32	
33	
34	def issue_id_for(issue_type: str, member_ids: list[str]) -> str:
35	    """Deterministic id for an issue, derived from its type and members.
36	
37	    Issues are recomputed fresh on every request rather than stored, so this
38	    id is what lets a dismissal survive across requests: as long as the same
39	    underlying data produces the same issue, it hashes to the same id.
40	    """
41	    key = f"{issue_type}|{','.join(sorted(member_ids))}"
42	    return hashlib.sha256(key.encode()).hexdigest()[:32]
43	
44	
45	def run_quality_checks(
46	    members: list[Member],
47	    relations: list[Relation],
48	    events: list[Event] | None = None,
49	    event_links: list[EventMemberLink] | None = None,
50	) -> list[dict]:
51	    events = events or []
52	    event_links = event_links or []
53	    issues: list[dict] = []
54	    member_map = {m.id: m for m in members}
55	
56	    # --- 1. Birth-after-death ---
57	    for m in members:
58	        birth = _year(m.date_of_birth)
59	        death = _year(m.date_of_death)
60	        if birth is not None and death is not None and birth > death:
61	            issues.append(
62	                {
63	                    "issue_type": "birth_after_death",
64	                    "severity": "error",
65	                    "member_ids": [m.id],
66	                    "description": f"Birth year ({birth}) is after death year ({death}).",
67	                }
68	            )
69	
70	    # --- 2. Parent–child age-gap anomalies ---
71	    # Relation direction: from_member_id = child, to_member_id = parent
72	    parent_pairs: list[tuple[str, str]] = [
73	        (r.to_member_id, r.from_member_id)  # (parent_id, child_id)
74	        for r in relations
75	        if r.relation_type == "parent"
76	    ]
77	
78	    for parent_id, child_id in parent_pairs:
79	        parent = member_map.get(parent_id)
80	        child = member_map.get(child_id)
81	        if parent is None or child is None:
82	            continue
83	        parent_birth = _year(parent.date_of_birth)
84	        parent_death = _year(parent.date_of_death)
85	        child_birth = _year(child.date_of_birth)
86	
87	        # Child born after the parent had already died. Fathers (and parents of
88	        # unknown gender) get a small posthumous-birth grace window; mothers get
89	        # none, since a birth after the mother's death is impossible.
90	        if parent_death is not None and child_birth is not None:
91	            is_mother = (parent.gender or "").lower() == "f"
92	            grace = 0 if is_mother else _POSTHUMOUS_BIRTH_GRACE_YEARS
93	            if child_birth > parent_death + grace:
94	                issues.append(
95	                    {
96	                        "issue_type": "child_after_parent_death",
97	                        "severity": "error",
98	                        "member_ids": [parent_id, child_id],
99	                        "description": (
100	                            f"Child was born ({child_birth}) after the "
101	                            f"parent's death year ({parent_death})."
102	                        ),
103	                    }
104	                )
105	
106	        if parent_birth is None or child_birth is None:
107	            continue
108	        age_at_birth = child_birth - parent_birth
109	        if age_at_birth < 0:
110	            issues.append(
111	                {
112	                    "issue_type": "child_older_than_parent",
113	                    "severity": "error",
114	                    "member_ids": [parent_id, child_id],
115	                    "description": (
116	                        f"Child's birth year ({child_birth}) is before "
117	                        f"parent's birth year ({parent_birth})."
118	                    ),
119	                }
120	            )
121	        elif age_at_birth < _MIN_PARENT_AGE:
122	            issues.append(
123	                {
124	                    "issue_type": "parent_too_young",
125	                    "severity": "warning",
126	                    "member_ids": [parent_id, child_id],
127	                    "description": (
128	                        f"Parent was only {age_at_birth} year(s) old when "
129	                        f"child was born ({child_birth})."
130	                    ),
131	                }
132	            )
133	        elif age_at_birth > _MAX_PARENT_AGE:
134	            issues.append(
135	                {
136	                    "issue_type": "parent_too_old",
137	                    "severity": "warning",
138	                    "member_ids": [parent_id, child_id],
139	                    "description": (
140	                        f"Parent was {age_at_birth} years old when "
141	                        f"child was born ({child_birth})."
142	                    ),
143	                }
144	            )
145	
146	    # --- 3. Relationship cycles (parent-chain) ---
147	    # Build child→parents adjacency for traversal.
148	    parents_of: dict[str, set[str]] = defaultdict(set)
149	    for parent_id, child_id in parent_pairs:
150	        parents_of[child_id].add(parent_id)
151	
152	    visited: set[str] = set()
153	    on_stack: set[str] = set()
154	    cycle_members: set[str] = set()
155	
156	    def _dfs(node: str) -> bool:
157	        visited.add(node)
158	        on_stack.add(node)
159	        for ancestor in parents_of.get(node, set()):
160	            if ancestor not in visited:
161	                if _dfs(ancestor):
162	                    cycle_members.update([node, ancestor])
163	                    return True
164	            elif ancestor in on_stack:
165	                cycle_members.update([node, ancestor])
166	                return True
167	        on_stack.discard(node)
168	        return False
169	
170	    for m in members:
171	        if m.id not in visited:
172	            _dfs(m.id)
173	
174	    if cycle_members:
175	        issues.append(
176	            {
177	                "issue_type": "relationship_cycle",
178	                "severity": "error",
179	                "member_ids": sorted(cycle_members),
180	                "description": "A cycle exists in the parent-child relationships.",
181	            }
182	        )
183	
184	    # --- 4. Duplicate-name candidates ---
185	    name_groups: dict[str, list[str]] = defaultdict(list)
186	    for m in members:
187	        first = (m.first_name or "").strip().lower()
188	        last = (m.last_name or "").strip().lower()
189	        if first or last:
190	            name_groups[f"{first}|{last}"].append(m.id)
191	
192	    for _key, ids in name_groups.items():
193	        if len(ids) > 1:
194	            issues.append(
195	                {
196	                    "issue_type": "duplicate_candidate",
197	                    "severity": "warning",
198	                    "member_ids": ids,
199	                    "description": f"{len(ids)} members share the same full name.",
200	                }
201	            )
202	
203	    # --- 5. Disconnected members (no relations at all) ---
204	    if len(members) > 1:
205	        connected: set[str] = set()
206	        for r in relations:
207	            connected.add(r.from_member_id)
208	            connected.add(r.to_member_id)
209	        for m in members:
210	            if m.id not in connected:
211	                issues.append(
212	                    {
213	                        "issue_type": "disconnected_member",
214	                        "severity": "warning",
215	                        "member_ids": [m.id],
216	                        "description": "Member has no relationships.",
217	                    }
218	                )
219	
220	    # --- 6. Event dated after the member's own death ---
221	    event_map = {e.id: e for e in events}
222	    for link in event_links:
223	        member = member_map.get(link.member_id)
224	        ev = event_map.get(link.event_id)
225	        if member is None or ev is None:
226	            continue
227	        if (ev.event_type or "").lower() in _POST_DEATH_EVENT_TYPES:
228	            continue
229	        death = _year(member.date_of_death)
230	        ev_year = _year(ev.date)
231	        if death is None or ev_year is None:
232	            continue
233	        if ev_year > death:
234	            issues.append(
235	                {
236	                    "id": issue_id_for("event_after_death", [member.id, ev.id]),
237	                    "issue_type": "event_after_death",
238	                    "severity": "warning",
239	                    "member_ids": [member.id],
240	                    "description": (
241	                        f"A '{ev.event_type}' event ({ev_year}) is dated after "
242	                        f"this member's death year ({death})."
243	                    ),
244	                }
245	            )
246	
247	    for issue in issues:
248	        issue.setdefault("id", issue_id_for(issue["issue_type"], issue["member_ids"]))
249	
250	    return issues
251

98	def _public_only(db: Session, tree: Tree, user: User | None) -> bool:

100	
101	
102	def _public_member_payloads(rows: list) -> list[dict]:
103	    return [PublicMemberOut(**row._mapping).model_dump(by_alias=True) for row in rows]
104	
105	
106	def _get_member(db: Session, tree: Tree, member_id: str) -> Member:
107	    member = db.get(Member, member_id)
108	    if member is None or member.tree_id != tree.id:
109	        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Member not found")
110	    return member
111	
112	
113	def _validate_linked_tree(
114	    db: Session, tree: Tree, user: User, linked_tree_id: str | None
115	) -> None:
116	    """Validate a tree-in-tree link target before it is persisted.
117	
118	    A null id (clearing the link) is always allowed. Otherwise the ``tree_links``
119	    feature must be enabled, the target must exist and be readable by the user,
120	    and a member may not link to its own tree.
121	    """
122	    if linked_tree_id is None:
123	        return
124	    from app.services import feature_service  # noqa: PLC0415
125	
126	    if not feature_service.is_enabled(db, "tree_links", user):
127	        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Not found")
128	    if linked_tree_id == tree.id:
129	        raise HTTPException(
130	            status_code=400, detail="A member cannot link to its own tree"
131	        )
132	    target = db.get(Tree, linked_tree_id)
133	    if target is None:
134	        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Linked tree not found")
135	    if (
136	        not user.is_admin
137	        and role_for(db, target, user) is None
138	        and target.public_role != "viewer"
139	    ):
140	        raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail="No access to linked tree")
141	
142	
143	def _validate_linked_member(
144	    db: Session,
145	    linked_tree_id: str | None,
146	    linked_member_id: str | None,
147	    member_id: str | None,
148	) -> None:
149	    """Validate the member-level counterpart of a tree-in-tree link.
150	
151	    ``linked_member_id`` identifies the row in the linked tree that represents
152	    the same person (the bridge person), so it must live inside
153	    ``linked_tree_id``. Access is already covered by ``_validate_linked_tree``.
154	    """
155	    if linked_member_id is None:
156	        return
157	    if linked_tree_id is None:
158	        raise HTTPException(
159	            status_code=400,
160	            detail="A linked member requires a linked tree",
161	        )
162	    if linked_member_id == member_id:
163	        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="A member cannot link to itself")
164	    target = db.get(Member, linked_member_id)
165	    if target is None or target.tree_id != linked_tree_id:
166	        raise HTTPException(
167	            status_code=400,
168	            detail="Linked member is not part of the linked tree",
169	        )
170	
171	
172	def _sync_bridge_person(
173	    db: Session, member: Member, changes: dict, user: User
174	) -> tuple[str | None, Tree | None]:
175	    """Mirror identity-field edits onto the counterpart row of a bridge person.
176	
177	    The two rows represent the same human, so person-level facts edited on one
178	    side propagate to the other — but only while the tree_links feature is
179	    enabled and the actor may write the counterpart's tree; otherwise the rows
180	    simply drift until edited from a side with access.
181	
182	    Returns ``(status, counterpart_tree)``: ``("synced", tree)`` when the
183	    counterpart was updated, ``("skipped_no_access", None)`` when identity
184	    fields changed but the actor may not write the other tree (the one case
185	    the editor should be told about), and ``(None, None)`` when there was
186	    nothing to sync (no link, no identity change, feature off, counterpart
187	    gone).
188	    """
189	    if member.linked_member_id is None:
190	        return None, None
191	    synced = {k: v for k, v in changes.items() if k in BRIDGE_SYNC_FIELDS}
192	    if not synced:
193	        return None, None
194	    from app.services import feature_service  # noqa: PLC0415
195	
196	    if not feature_service.is_enabled(db, "tree_links", user):
197	        return None, None
198	    counterpart = db.get(Member, member.linked_member_id)
199	    if counterpart is None:
200	        return None, None
201	    target_tree = db.get(Tree, counterpart.tree_id)
202	    if target_tree is None:
203	        return None, None
204	    if not user.is_admin and role_for(db, target_tree, user) not in (
205	        "owner",
206	        "editor",
207	    ):
208	        return "skipped_no_access", None
209	    for key, value in synced.items():
210	        if key == "image_data" and value:
211	            # Media files are tree-scoped: copy the file into the
212	            # counterpart's tree instead of sharing the URL across trees.
213	            value = copy_media_to_tree(value, counterpart.tree_id)
214	        setattr(counterpart, key, value)
215	    return "synced", target_tree

531	def _sync_parent_slots(
532	    db: Session,
533	    tree: Tree,
534	    member: Member,
535	    paternal_changed: bool,
536	    paternal_parent_id: str | None,
537	    maternal_changed: bool,
538	    maternal_parent_id: str | None,
539	) -> None:
540	    """Apply explicit parent-slot changes without touching extra parent rows.
541	
542	    The persisted relation model has no slot column.  We reconstruct the two
543	    slots with the same gender-first rule as the frontend, then replace only a
544	    slot the request explicitly changed.  Replaying the same payload is a
545	    no-op, which keeps retries idempotent.
546	    """
547	    relations = list(
548	        db.scalars(
549	            select(Relation).where(
550	                Relation.tree_id == tree.id,
551	                Relation.from_member_id == member.id,
552	                Relation.relation_type == "parent",
553	            )
554	        ).all()
555	    )
556	    parent_ids = [relation.to_member_id for relation in relations]
557	    parents = {
558	        parent.id: parent
559	        for parent in db.scalars(
560	            select(Member).where(Member.tree_id == tree.id, Member.id.in_(parent_ids))
561	        ).all()
562	    }
563	
564	    paternal_current: str | None = None
565	    maternal_current: str | None = None
566	    for parent_id in parent_ids:
567	        gender = parents.get(parent_id).gender if parent_id in parents else None
568	        if gender == "m" and paternal_current is None:
569	            paternal_current = parent_id
570	        elif gender == "f" and maternal_current is None:
571	            maternal_current = parent_id
572	    for parent_id in parent_ids:
573	        if parent_id in {paternal_current, maternal_current}:
574	            continue
575	        if paternal_current is None:
576	            paternal_current = parent_id
577	        elif maternal_current is None:
578	            maternal_current = parent_id
579	
580	    for changed, previous, replacement in (
581	        (paternal_changed, paternal_current, paternal_parent_id),
582	        (maternal_changed, maternal_current, maternal_parent_id),
583	    ):
584	        if not changed:
585	            continue
586	        if replacement == previous:
587	            continue
588	        if previous is not None:
589	            relation = db.get(Relation, (tree.id, member.id, previous, "parent"))
590	            if relation is not None:
591	                db.delete(relation)
592	        if replacement is None:
593	            continue
594	        parent = parents.get(replacement)
595	        if parent is None:
596	            parent = db.scalar(
597	                select(Member).where(
598	                    Member.id == replacement,
599	                    Member.tree_id == tree.id,
600	                )
601	            )
602	        if parent is None:
603	            raise HTTPException(
604	                status_code=404, detail="parent_id not found in this tree"
605	            )
606	        if db.get(Relation, (tree.id, member.id, replacement, "parent")) is None:
607	            db.add(
608	                Relation(
609	                    tree_id=tree.id,
610	                    from_member_id=member.id,
611	                    to_member_id=replacement,
612	                    relation_type="parent",
613	                )
614	            )
615

617	def _sync_vital_event(
618	    db: Session,
619	    tree: Tree,
620	    member: Member,
621	    event_type: str,
622	    date: str | None,
623	    location: str | None,
624	) -> None:
625	    """Keep one member's birth/death event aligned without losing documents."""
626	    events = list(
627	        db.scalars(
628	            select(Event)
629	            .join(EventMemberLink, EventMemberLink.event_id == Event.id)
630	            .where(
631	                Event.tree_id == tree.id,
632	                Event.event_type == event_type,
633	                EventMemberLink.member_id == member.id,
634	            )
635	            .order_by(Event.id)
636	        ).all()
637	    )
638	    existing = events[0] if events else None
639	    if date:
640	        if existing is not None:
641	            # Do not replace the row: its description and linked documents
642	            # are user-authored details preserved by #659. The location is
643	            # only backfilled while still empty, so an existing (possibly
644	            # user-authored) location is never silently overwritten (#769).
645	            existing.date = date
646	            if location and not existing.location:
647	                existing.location = location
648	            return
649	        event = Event(
650	            id=str(uuid4()),
651	            tree_id=tree.id,
652	            event_type=event_type,
653	            date=date,
654	            location=location,
655	            created_at=utcnow_iso(),
656	        )
657	        db.add(event)
658	        db.flush()
659	        db.add(EventMemberLink(event_id=event.id, member_id=member.id))
660	    elif existing is not None:
661	        db.delete(existing)

664	@router.patch("/members/{member_id}", response_model=MemberOut)
665	def update_member(
666	    member_id: str,
667	    payload: MemberUpdate,
668	    tree: Tree = Depends(get_writable_tree),
669	    user: User = Depends(get_current_user),
670	    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
671	):
672	    member = _get_member(db, tree, member_id)
673	    changes = payload.model_dump(exclude_unset=True)
674	    paternal_changed = "paternal_parent_id" in changes
675	    maternal_changed = "maternal_parent_id" in changes
676	    paternal_parent_id = changes.pop("paternal_parent_id", None)
677	    maternal_parent_id = changes.pop("maternal_parent_id", None)
678	    # The member form re-sends the link fields unchanged on every save. Only an
679	    # actual change is a link edit — an unchanged value must not re-run the
680	    # feature/access checks, otherwise ordinary edits fail once the tree_links
681	    # flag is turned off (or for editors without access to the linked tree).
682	    if "linked_tree_id" in changes and changes["linked_tree_id"] == member.linked_tree_id:
683	        del changes["linked_tree_id"]
684	    if (
685	        "linked_member_id" in changes
686	        and changes["linked_member_id"] == member.linked_member_id
687	    ):
688	        del changes["linked_member_id"]
689	    unlinked_counterpart_tree: Tree | None = None
690	    if "linked_tree_id" in changes:
691	        if changes["linked_tree_id"] is not None:
692	            # Establishing a link requires resolving a bridge person on both
693	            # sides, which touches two trees — this single-row endpoint can't
694	            # do that safely. Only clearing (null) or leaving it unchanged is
695	            # allowed here; see POST /members/{id}/link.
696	            raise HTTPException(
697	                status_code=400,
698	                detail="Establish tree links via the link endpoint",
699	            )
700	        _validate_linked_tree(db, tree, user, changes["linked_tree_id"])
701	        # Unlinking invalidates the counterpart pointer into the old tree.
702	        changes["linked_member_id"] = None
703	        # Tear down the other side too: a bridge is symmetric, so unlinking
704	        # here must also clear the counterpart's fields. Otherwise the link
705	        # lingers in the other tree (phantom badge) and identity edits keep
706	        # flowing one-directionally from the still-linked counterpart back to
707	        # this member. Cleared unconditionally, like the delete path — this is
708	        # integrity cleanup of a now-broken bridge, not a content edit.
709	        if member.linked_member_id is not None:
710	            counterpart = db.get(Member, member.linked_member_id)
711	            if counterpart is not None:
712	                counterpart.linked_tree_id = None
713	                counterpart.linked_member_id = None
714	                unlinked_counterpart_tree = db.get(Tree, counterpart.tree_id)
715	    if changes.get("linked_member_id") is not None:
716	        _validate_linked_member(
717	            db,
718	            changes.get("linked_tree_id", member.linked_tree_id),
719	            changes["linked_member_id"],
720	            member.id,
721	        )
722	    new_image_url: str | None = None
723	    if "image_data" in changes:
724	        try:
725	            new_url = process_image_field(
726	                tree.id,
727	                changes["image_data"],
728	                get_media_limits(db),
729	            )
730	            changes["image_data"] = new_url
731	            if new_url and new_url.startswith(MEDIA_URL_PREFIX):
732	                new_image_url = new_url
733	        except ImageTooLarge as exc:
734	            raise HTTPException(status_code=413, detail=str(exc)) from exc
735	        except (UnsupportedImageType, ValueError) as exc:
736	            raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail=str(exc)) from exc
737	
738	    # Check media quota for the new image (write-then-verify: file already on
739	    # disk and counted by compute_usage, so pass 0 to avoid double-counting).
740	    if new_image_url:
741	        try:
742	            check_media_quota(db, tree, 0)
743	        except QuotaExceeded as exc:
744	            delete_media(new_image_url)
745	            raise HTTPException(status_code=413, detail=str(exc)) from exc
746	    # Capture before-state for diff details (skip noisy positional/internal fields).
747	    _SKIP_DIFF = {"position_x", "position_y", "is_collapsed", "image_data"}
748	    before = {k: getattr(member, k) for k in changes if k not in _SKIP_DIFF}
749	    for key, value in changes.items():
750	        setattr(member, key, value)
751	    if paternal_changed or maternal_changed:
752	        _sync_parent_slots(
753	            db,
754	            tree,
755	            member,
756	            paternal_changed,
757	            paternal_parent_id,
758	            maternal_changed,
759	            maternal_parent_id,
760	        )
761	    vital_events_changed = _event_updates_allowed(db, tree, user) and (
762	        "date_of_birth" in changes
763	        or "date_of_death" in changes
764	        or "birthplace" in changes
765	        or "cemetery" in changes
766	    )
767	    if vital_events_changed:
768	        # member fields above are already mutated by the setattr loop, so the
769	        # current date/place reflect this save even when only one of the pair
770	        # (e.g. birthplace without a date change) was actually sent.
771	        if "date_of_birth" in changes or "birthplace" in changes:
772	            _sync_vital_event(
773	                db, tree, member, "birth", member.date_of_birth, member.birthplace
774	            )
775	        if "date_of_death" in changes or "cemetery" in changes:
776	            _sync_vital_event(

882	@router.get(
883	    "/members/{member_id}/link-candidates",
884	    response_model=LinkCandidatesOut,
885	)
886	def get_link_candidates(
887	    member_id: str,
888	    target_tree_id: str = Query(...),
889	    tree: Tree = Depends(get_writable_tree),
890	    user: User = Depends(get_current_user),
891	    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
892	):
893	    """List same-named members of ``target_tree_id`` that could be the bridge
894	    counterpart for ``member_id`` — i.e. candidates for ``POST .../link``
895	    with ``mode="existing"``.
896	
897	    Only members matching the source member's name+gender key are returned
898	    (a bridge person is the same human on both sides, so an unrelated match
899	    would be meaningless), excluding the source member itself and anyone
900	    already linked to another tree. Each candidate is shaped as a
901	    ``DuplicatePair`` (reusing the tree-merge machinery) so the client can
902	    render the same conflict-resolution UI merge already uses.
903	    """
904	    from app.services import feature_service  # noqa: PLC0415
905	    from app.services.merge import (  # noqa: PLC0415
906	        compute_conflicts,
907	        member_key,
908	        member_name_key,
909	    )
910	
911	    if not feature_service.is_enabled(db, "tree_links", user):
912	        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Not found")
913	    member = _get_member(db, tree, member_id)
914	
915	    _validate_linked_tree(db, tree, user, target_tree_id)
916	    target = db.get(Tree, target_tree_id)
917	    if target is None:
918	        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Linked tree not found")
919	    # Candidates are only useful if the caller can actually link one, which
920	    # requires write access to the target (same check the link endpoint uses).
921	    if not user.is_admin and role_for(db, target, user) not in ("owner", "editor"):
922	        raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail="No write access to the linked tree")
923	
924	    source_name_key = member_name_key(member)
925	    source_exact_key = member_key(member)
926	    candidates: list[DuplicatePair] = []
927	    for candidate in db.scalars(select(Member).where(Member.tree_id == target.id)):
928	        if candidate.id == member.id:
929	            continue
930	        if candidate.linked_tree_id is not None:
931	            continue
932	        if member_name_key(candidate) != source_name_key:
933	            continue
934	        match = "exact" if member_key(candidate) == source_exact_key else "possible"
935	        candidates.append(
936	            DuplicatePair(
937	                member_a=MemberOut.model_validate(member),
938	                member_b=MemberOut.model_validate(candidate),
939	                match=match,
940	                conflicts=compute_conflicts(member, candidate),
941	                default_action="merge",
942	            )
943	        )
944	    return LinkCandidatesOut(candidates=candidates)
