947	@router.post(
948	    "/members/{member_id}/link",
949	    response_model=MemberSubtreeOut,
950	    status_code=201,
951	)
952	def link_member_to_tree(
953	    member_id: str,
954	    payload: MemberLinkRequest,
955	    tree: Tree = Depends(get_writable_tree),
956	    user: User = Depends(get_current_user),
957	    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
958	):
959	    """Establish a tree-in-tree bridge between this member and a target tree.
960	
961	    Unlike ``PATCH /members/{id}`` (which can only clear a link, never create
962	    one — see the loophole this closes), this endpoint always resolves a real
963	    bridge person on both sides: either an existing member the caller asserts
964	    is the same person (``mode="existing"``), or a fresh clone seeded into the
965	    target tree (``mode="create"``). Establishing a link writes rows in two
966	    trees, so it requires write access to both.
967	    """
968	    from app.services import feature_service  # noqa: PLC0415
969	    from app.services.merge import _clone_member, _wire_bridge  # noqa: PLC0415
970	
971	    if not feature_service.is_enabled(db, "tree_links", user):
972	        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Not found")
973	    member = _get_member(db, tree, member_id)
974	    if member.linked_tree_id is not None:
975	        raise HTTPException(status_code=409, detail="Member is already linked to a tree")
976	
977	    _validate_linked_tree(db, tree, user, payload.linked_tree_id)
978	    target = db.get(Tree, payload.linked_tree_id)
979	    if target is None:
980	        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Linked tree not found")
981	    # Establishing a bridge writes the counterpart row too, so read access to
982	    # the target (already checked by _validate_linked_tree) is not enough.
983	    if not user.is_admin and role_for(db, target, user) not in ("owner", "editor"):
984	        raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail="No write access to the linked tree")
985	
986	    if payload.mode == "create":
987	        counterpart = _clone_member(member, target.id, str(uuid4()))
988	        counterpart.position_x = 0
989	        counterpart.position_y = 0
990	        counterpart.is_collapsed = False
991	        db.add(counterpart)
992	        db.flush()
993	    else:
994	        if payload.counterpart_member_id is None:
995	            raise HTTPException(
996	                status_code=400,
997	                detail="counterpart_member_id is required for mode=existing",
998	            )
999	        counterpart = db.get(Member, payload.counterpart_member_id)
1000	        if counterpart is None or counterpart.tree_id != target.id:
1001	            raise HTTPException(
1002	                status_code=400,
1003	                detail="Counterpart member is not part of the linked tree",
1004	            )
1005	        if counterpart.id == member.id:
1006	            raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="A member cannot link to itself")
1007	        if counterpart.linked_tree_id is not None:
1008	            raise HTTPException(
1009	                status_code=400,
1010	                detail="Counterpart member is already linked to a tree",
1011	            )
1012	
1013	    _wire_bridge(member, counterpart)
1014	    if payload.mode == "existing":
1015	        # The two rows may describe the same person with differing details
1016	        # (dates, places, notes, ...) — reconcile them onto both sides now
1017	        # rather than letting the bridge start out of sync. field_choices is
1018	        # ignored for mode="create": the counterpart there is a fresh clone of
1019	        # `member`, so there is nothing to reconcile.
1020	        from app.services.merge import reconcile_bridge_fields  # noqa: PLC0415
1021	
1022	        reconcile_bridge_fields(member, counterpart, payload.field_choices)
1023	
1024	    label = " ".join(filter(None, [member.first_name, member.last_name])) or None
1025	    record_activity(
1026	        db,
1027	        tree_id=tree.id,
1028	        actor=user,
1029	        action="update",
1030	        target_type="member",
1031	        target_id=member.id,
1032	        target_label=label,
1033	        details={"after": {"linked_tree_id": target.id}},
1034	    )
1035	    counterpart_label = (
1036	        " ".join(filter(None, [counterpart.first_name, counterpart.last_name])) or None
1037	    )
1038	    if payload.mode == "create":
1039	        record_activity(
1040	            db,
1041	            tree_id=target.id,
1042	            actor=user,
1043	            action="create",
1044	            target_type="member",
1045	            target_id=counterpart.id,
1046	            target_label=counterpart_label,
1047	        )
1048	    else:
1049	        record_activity(
1050	            db,
1051	            tree_id=target.id,
1052	            actor=user,
1053	            action="update",
1054	            target_type="member",
1055	            target_id=counterpart.id,
1056	            target_label=counterpart_label,
1057	            details={"after": {"linked_tree_id": tree.id}},
1058	        )
1059	    db.commit()
1060	    publish_tree_event(db, tree, "activity.entry_added", {"tree_id": tree.id})
1061	    publish_tree_event(db, target, "activity.entry_added", {"tree_id": target.id})
1062	    db.refresh(member)
1063	    db.refresh(target)
1064	    publish_tree_event(
1065	        db,
1066	        tree,
1067	        "tree.content_changed",
1068	        {"tree_id": tree.id, "domain": "member"},
1069	    )
1070	    invalidate_stats(tree.id)
1071	    publish_tree_event(
1072	        db,
1073	        target,
1074	        "tree.content_changed",
1075	        {"tree_id": target.id, "domain": "member"},
1076	    )
1077	    invalidate_stats(target.id)
1078	    return MemberSubtreeOut(
1079	        tree=TreeOut.model_validate(target),
1080	        anchor=MemberOut.model_validate(member),
1081	    )

1089	    user: User = Depends(get_current_user),
1090	    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
1091	):
1092	    """Resolve bridge-person drift by copying person-level fields across the
1093	    link: ``push`` writes this member's values onto the counterpart, ``pull``
1094	    adopts the counterpart's values. Requires write access to both trees.
1095	    """
1096	    from app.services import feature_service  # noqa: PLC0415
1097	
1098	    if not feature_service.is_enabled(db, "tree_links", user):
1099	        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Not found")
1100	    member = _get_member(db, tree, member_id)
1101	    if member.linked_member_id is None:
1102	        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="Member has no linked member")
1103	    counterpart = db.get(Member, member.linked_member_id)
1104	    if counterpart is None:
1105	        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Linked member not found")
1106	    other_tree = db.get(Tree, counterpart.tree_id)
1107	    if other_tree is None:
1108	        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Linked tree not found")
1109	    if not user.is_admin and role_for(db, other_tree, user) not in (
1110	        "owner",
1111	        "editor",
1112	    ):
1113	        raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail="No write access to linked tree")
1114	
1115	    src, dst = (
1116	        (member, counterpart) if payload.direction == "push" else (counterpart, member)
1117	    )
1118	    copy_bridge_fields(src, dst)
1119	
1120	    label = " ".join(filter(None, [member.first_name, member.last_name])) or None
1121	    record_activity(
1122	        db,
1123	        tree_id=tree.id,
1124	        actor=user,
1125	        action="update",
1126	        target_type="member",
1127	        target_id=member.id,
1128	        target_label=label,
1129	        details={"after": {"bridge_sync": payload.direction}},
1130	    )
1131	    db.commit()
1132	    publish_tree_event(db, tree, "activity.entry_added", {"tree_id": tree.id})
1133	    db.refresh(member)
1134	    for t in (tree, other_tree):
1135	        publish_tree_event(
1136	            db,
1137	            t,
1138	            "tree.content_changed",
1139	            {"tree_id": t.id, "domain": "member"},
1140	        )
1141	        invalidate_stats(t.id)

"""Data-quality report endpoint."""

import json

from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, HTTPException
from sqlalchemy import select
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from app.api.deps import (
    get_current_user,
    get_readable_tree,
    get_writable_tree,
    require_feature,
)
from app.db.session import get_db
from app.models import Tree, User
from app.models.content import Event, EventMemberLink
from app.models.family import Member, Relation
from app.models.quality import QualityIssueDismissal
from app.schemas.quality import QualityIssue, QualityReport
from app.services.bridge import drift_fields
from app.services.quality_checks import issue_id_for, run_quality_checks

router = APIRouter(
    prefix="/trees/{tree_id}",
    tags=["quality"],
    dependencies=[Depends(require_feature("quality_report"))],
)


def _bridge_drift_issues(
    db: Session, user: User, members: list[Member]
) -> list[dict]:
    """Bridge persons whose two rows have drifted apart.

    Needs the db (counterpart rows live in other trees), so it runs here
    rather than in the pure ``run_quality_checks``. The comparison happens
    server-side only — field *names* are reported, never the other tree's
    values — and the whole check is dormant while tree_links is off.
    """
    linked = [m for m in members if m.linked_member_id]
    if not linked:
        return []
    from app.services import feature_service  # noqa: PLC0415

    if not feature_service.is_enabled(db, "tree_links", user):
        return []
    counterparts = {
        c.id: c
        for c in db.scalars(
            select(Member).where(
                Member.id.in_([m.linked_member_id for m in linked])
            )
        )
    }
    issues: list[dict] = []
    for m in linked:
        counterpart = counterparts.get(m.linked_member_id)
        if counterpart is None:
            continue
        fields = drift_fields(m, counterpart)
        if not fields:
            continue
        issues.append(
            {
                # Hash the drifted field set too, so a dismissed note comes
                # back when *new* fields start to differ.
                "id": issue_id_for("bridge_person_drift", [m.id, *fields]),
                "issue_type": "bridge_person_drift",
                "severity": "warning",
                "member_ids": [m.id],
                "description": (
                    "Differs from the linked copy in another tree: "
                    f"{', '.join(f.replace('_', ' ') for f in fields)}."
                ),
            }
        )
    return issues


@router.get("/quality-report", response_model=QualityReport)
def get_quality_report(
    include_dismissed: bool = False,
    tree: Tree = Depends(get_readable_tree),
    user: User = Depends(get_current_user),
    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
):
    """Return a non-destructive data-quality report for the tree.

    Accessible to anyone with at least read access. Dismissed issues are
    excluded by default; pass ``include_dismissed=true`` to get the full
    list with each issue's ``dismissed`` flag set.
    """
    members = list(db.scalars(select(Member).where(Member.tree_id == tree.id)).all())
    relations = list(
        db.scalars(select(Relation).where(Relation.tree_id == tree.id)).all()
    )
    events = list(db.scalars(select(Event).where(Event.tree_id == tree.id)).all())
    event_links = list(
        db.scalars(
            select(EventMemberLink)
            .join(Event, Event.id == EventMemberLink.event_id)
            .where(Event.tree_id == tree.id)
        ).all()
    )
    raw_issues = run_quality_checks(members, relations, events, event_links)
    raw_issues += _bridge_drift_issues(db, user, members)

    dismissed_ids = set(
        db.scalars(
            select(QualityIssueDismissal.issue_id).where(
                QualityIssueDismissal.tree_id == tree.id
            )
        ).all()
    )

    issues = [QualityIssue(**i, dismissed=i["id"] in dismissed_ids) for i in raw_issues]
    if not include_dismissed:
        issues = [i for i in issues if not i.dismissed]

    return QualityReport(
        tree_id=tree.id,
        total_members=len(members),
        issues=issues,
    )


@router.post("/quality-report/issues/{issue_id}/dismiss", status_code=204)
def dismiss_quality_issue(
    issue_id: str,
    tree: Tree = Depends(get_writable_tree),
    user: User = Depends(get_current_user),
    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
):
    """Dismiss a quality issue so it no longer shows up by default.

    The issue must currently exist (i.e. be produced by the live checks) to
    be dismissable. Dismissals are tree-scoped and shared by every editor.
    """
    existing = db.scalar(
        select(QualityIssueDismissal).where(
            QualityIssueDismissal.tree_id == tree.id,
            QualityIssueDismissal.issue_id == issue_id,
        )
    )
    if existing is not None:
        return None

    members = list(db.scalars(select(Member).where(Member.tree_id == tree.id)).all())
    relations = list(
        db.scalars(select(Relation).where(Relation.tree_id == tree.id)).all()
    )
    events = list(db.scalars(select(Event).where(Event.tree_id == tree.id)).all())
    event_links = list(
        db.scalars(
            select(EventMemberLink)
            .join(Event, Event.id == EventMemberLink.event_id)
            .where(Event.tree_id == tree.id)
        ).all()
    )
    raw_issues = run_quality_checks(members, relations, events, event_links)
    issue = next((i for i in raw_issues if i["id"] == issue_id), None)
    if issue is None:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Quality issue not found")

    db.add(
        QualityIssueDismissal(
            tree_id=tree.id,
            issue_id=issue["id"],
            issue_type=issue["issue_type"],
            member_ids=json.dumps(issue["member_ids"]),
            dismissed_by_id=user.id,
        )
    )
    db.commit()
    return None


@router.delete("/quality-report/issues/{issue_id}/dismiss", status_code=204)
def restore_quality_issue(
    issue_id: str,
    tree: Tree = Depends(get_writable_tree),
    db: Session = Depends(get_db),
):
    """Undo a previous dismissal so the issue shows up again by default."""
    dismissal = db.scalar(
        select(QualityIssueDismissal).where(
            QualityIssueDismissal.tree_id == tree.id,
            QualityIssueDismissal.issue_id == issue_id,
        )
    )
    if dismissal is not None:
        db.delete(dismissal)
        db.commit()
    return None

) -> dict:
    """Full pre-image of a member row and its cascade children.

    Must be called BEFORE ``db.delete(member)``. Captures everything the DB
    cascade will remove: relations on either side, disease records, and the
    five content link tables (research-task rows themselves survive a member
    delete; only their links cascade). ``counterpart`` is the bridge person in the
    linked tree whose link pointers the delete route dissolves; its identity
    is recorded so the tree-in-tree link can be re-established on undo.
    Virtual-view match rows also cascade but are derived state the matching
    service recomputes, so they are deliberately not snapshotted.
    """
    relations = db.scalars(
        select(Relation).where(
            or_(
                Relation.from_member_id == member.id,
                Relation.to_member_id == member.id,
            )
        )
    ).all()
    diseases = db.scalars(
        select(MemberDisease).where(MemberDisease.member_id == member.id)
    ).all()
    tables: dict[str, object] = {
        "member": row_to_dict(member),
        "relations": [row_to_dict(r) for r in relations],
        "diseases": [row_to_dict(d) for d in diseases],
    }
    for key, model in (
        ("task_links", MemberTaskLink),
        ("event_links", EventMemberLink),
        ("story_links", StoryMemberLink),
        ("gallery_links", GalleryMemberLink),
        ("document_links", DocumentMemberLink),
    ):
        rows = db.scalars(select(model).where(model.member_id == member.id)).all()
        tables[key] = [row_to_dict(r) for r in rows]
    if counterpart is not None:
        tables["bridge"] = {
            "counterpart_member_id": counterpart.id,
            "counterpart_tree_id": counterpart.tree_id,
        }
    return delete_snapshot(**tables)


def record_activity(
    db: Session,
    *,
    tree_id: str,
    actor: User,
    action: str,
    target_type: str,
    target_id: str | None = None,
    target_label: str | None = None,
    details: dict | None = None,
) -> None:
    db.add(
        ActivityLog(
            tree_id=tree_id,
            actor_id=actor.id,
            actor_username=actor.username,
            action=action,
            target_type=target_type,
            target_id=target_id,
            target_label=target_label,
            details=json.dumps(details) if details is not None else None,
        )
    )

"""Core genealogy tables."""

from sqlalchemy import Boolean, Float, ForeignKey, String, Text
from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column, validates

from app.db.base import Base


class Member(Base):
    __tablename__ = "members"

    id: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(36), primary_key=True)
    tree_id: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(
        String(36), ForeignKey("trees.id", ondelete="CASCADE"), index=True
    )

    gender: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(String(1), nullable=True)
    academic_title: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(String(100), nullable=True)
    first_name: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(String(255), nullable=True)
    middle_names: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(String(255), nullable=True)
    baptismal_name: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(String(255), nullable=True)
    last_name: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(String(255), nullable=True)
    maiden_name: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(String(255), nullable=True)
    # Relative media URL (e.g. /api/media/<tree>/<file>) or null.
    image_data: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(Text, nullable=True)
    date_of_birth: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(String(40), nullable=True)
    date_of_death: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(String(40), nullable=True)
    date_of_birth_sort: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(
        String(10), nullable=True, index=True
    )
    date_of_death_sort: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(
        String(10), nullable=True, index=True
    )
    additional_data: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(Text, nullable=True)
    birthplace: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(String(255), nullable=True)
    hometown: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(String(255), nullable=True)
    cemetery: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(String(255), nullable=True)
    places_lived: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(Text, nullable=True)
    deceased: Mapped[bool] = mapped_column(Boolean, default=False, nullable=False)
    adopted: Mapped[bool] = mapped_column(Boolean, default=False, nullable=False)
    is_collapsed: Mapped[bool] = mapped_column(Boolean, default=False)
    # Optional pointer to another tree that details this person's own family
    # (the "tree-in-tree" link). SET NULL so deleting the target tree just
    # clears the link rather than cascading.
    linked_tree_id: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(
        String(36),
        ForeignKey("trees.id", ondelete="SET NULL"),
        nullable=True,
        index=True,
    )
    # The counterpart row in the linked tree representing the same person (the
    # "bridge person"). Navigation into the linked tree centers on it. SET NULL
    # so deleting the counterpart degrades the link to tree-level only.
    linked_member_id: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(
        String(36),
        ForeignKey("members.id", ondelete="SET NULL"),
        nullable=True,
        index=True,
    )
    position_x: Mapped[float] = mapped_column(Float, default=0)
    position_y: Mapped[float] = mapped_column(Float, default=0)

    @validates("date_of_birth", "date_of_death")
    def _derive_date_sort(self, key: str, value: str | None) -> str | None:
        """Automatically keep the ``*_sort`` columns in sync with date changes.

        Called by SQLAlchemy whenever ``date_of_birth`` or ``date_of_death`` is
        assigned, including on ``__init__``, ``setattr``-based updates, and
        bulk-attribute updates.  The sort key is derived lazily to avoid an
        import at module load time.
        """
        # Lazy import to prevent any potential circular-import issues at
        # module load time (genealogy_date has no DB imports, but being
        # defensive is cheap here).
        from app.services.genealogy_date import sort_key  # noqa: PLC0415

        setattr(self, f"{key}_sort", sort_key(value))
        return value


class Relation(Base):
    __tablename__ = "relations"

    tree_id: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(
        String(36), ForeignKey("trees.id", ondelete="CASCADE"), primary_key=True
    )
    from_member_id: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(
        String(36), ForeignKey("members.id", ondelete="CASCADE"), primary_key=True
    )
    to_member_id: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(
        String(36), ForeignKey("members.id", ondelete="CASCADE"), primary_key=True
    )
    relation_type: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(50), primary_key=True)


class RelationType(Base):
    """Instance-wide registry of relation types, managed by admins."""

    __tablename__ = "relation_types"

    id: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(50), primary_key=True)
    description: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(String(255), nullable=True)
    label: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(String(255), nullable=True)
    color: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(String(64), nullable=True)
    stroke_width: Mapped[float | None] = mapped_column(Float, nullable=True)
    stroke_dasharray: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(String(32), nullable=True)


class MemberDisease(Base):
    __tablename__ = "member_diseases"

    id: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(36), primary_key=True)
    tree_id: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(
        String(36), ForeignKey("trees.id", ondelete="CASCADE"), index=True
    )
    member_id: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(
        String(36), ForeignKey("members.id", ondelete="CASCADE"), index=True
    )
    name: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(255))
    carrier_status: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(50))
    inheritance_pattern: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(50), default="unknown")
    diagnosis_date: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(String(40), nullable=True)
    notes: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(Text, nullable=True)

"""Schemas for the merge-preview and resolution endpoints."""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Literal

from pydantic import BaseModel

from app.schemas.family import MemberOut


class TreeMergePreviewRequest(BaseModel):
    source_a: str
    source_b: str | None = None


class DuplicatePair(BaseModel):
    member_a: MemberOut
    member_b: MemberOut
    match: Literal["exact", "possible"]
    conflicts: list[str]
    default_action: Literal["merge", "keep_both"]


class TreeMergePreview(BaseModel):
    total_members: int
    merged_count: int
    duplicates: list[DuplicatePair]


class LinkCandidatesOut(BaseModel):
    """Same-named members in a target tree that could be the bridge
    counterpart for a tree-in-tree link, shaped like merge duplicate pairs so
    the client can reuse ``MergeConflictResolver``."""

    candidates: list[DuplicatePair]


# --- Resolution types (used in the merge request) --------------------------


class MergeResolution(BaseModel):
    member_a_id: str
    member_b_id: str
    action: Literal["merge", "keep_both"] = "merge"
    fields: dict[str, Literal["a", "b", "combine"]] = {}

15	/**
16	 * Fields that can be chosen / combined when resolving merge conflicts.
17	 * Mirrors the backend's _CONFLICT_FIELDS list.
18	 */

20	  "middleNames",

22	  "maidenName",

31	];
32	
33	/**
34	 * Fields for which the "Combine" option makes sense (free-form text).
35	 */
36	export const COMBINABLE_FIELDS: readonly string[] = [
37	  "additionalData",
38	  "placesLived",
39	];
40	
41	/**
42	 * Per-pair UI state that the user fills in during the resolve step.
43	 */
44	export interface PairResolutionState {
45	  action: "merge" | "keep_both";
46	  /** Only relevant when action === "merge". */
47	  fields: Partial<Record<string, MergeFieldChoice>>;
48	}
49	
50	/**
51	 * Build the initial resolution state for a duplicate pair from the backend's
52	 * `default_action` suggestion and its conflict list.
53	 */
54	export function buildInitialResolutionState(
55	  pair: DuplicatePair,
56	): PairResolutionState {
57	  const fields: Partial<Record<string, MergeFieldChoice>> = {};
58	  for (const field of pair.conflicts) {
59	    // Default field choice: "a" (keep source-A value)
60	    fields[field] = "a";
61	  }
62	  return {
63	    action: pair.default_action,
64	    fields,
65	  };
66	}
67	
68	/**
69	 * Convert the map of per-pair UI state into the `resolutions` array expected
70	 * by POST /trees/merge.
71	 *
72	 * Only pairs that are not using the server default need a resolution entry,
73	 * but we send all to keep the logic simple.
74	 */
75	export function buildResolutionsPayload(
76	  pairs: DuplicatePair[],
77	  states: Map<string, PairResolutionState>,
78	): MergeResolution[] {
79	  return pairs.map((pair) => {
80	    const pairKey = buildPairKey(pair.member_a.id, pair.member_b.id);
81	    const state = states.get(pairKey) ?? buildInitialResolutionState(pair);
82	    return {
83	      member_a_id: pair.member_a.id,
84	      member_b_id: pair.member_b.id,
85	      action: state.action,
86	      fields: state.action === "merge" ? { ...state.fields } : {},
87	    };
88	  });
89	}
90	
91	/**
92	 * A stable string key for a pair that is order-insensitive.
93	 */
94	export function buildPairKey(idA: string, idB: string): string {
95	  return [idA, idB].sort().join("|");
96	}
97	
98	/**
99	 * Human-readable display label for a member (first + last name).
100	 */
101	export function memberDisplayName(m: MemberDB): string {
102	  return [m.firstName, m.lastName].filter(Boolean).join(" ") || "(unknown)";
103	}
104	
105	/**
106	 * Return the value of a named field from a MemberDB record.
107	 */
108	export function getMemberField(
109	  member: MemberDB,
110	  field: string,
111	): string | null | undefined {
112	  return (member as unknown as Record<string, unknown>)[field] as
113	    | string
114	    | null
115	    | undefined;
116	}
117	
118	/**
119	 * Return true when both member values are non-empty and differ.
120	 * Used to decide whether to show a highlighted conflict badge.
121	 */
122	export function isFieldConflicting(
123	  pair: DuplicatePair,
124	  field: string,
125	): boolean {
126	  return pair.conflicts.includes(field);

"""Tests for compute_merge_preview and the resolution-aware merge_trees.

These are *in addition* to the existing test_merge.py tests (which are left
untouched to verify backward compatibility).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import pytest
from fastapi import HTTPException

from app.models import Member, Relation
from app.schemas.merge import MergeResolution
from app.services.merge import compute_merge_preview, merge_trees
from tests.conftest import add_member, make_tree, make_user, share

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Preview helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_preview_exact_duplicates(db):
    user = make_user(db, "alice")
    ta = make_tree(db, user, "A")
    tb = make_tree(db, user, "B")

    add_member(db, ta, "a1", first_name="Henry", last_name="Miller", gender="m",
               date_of_birth="1920", additional_data="Note A", birthplace="Berlin")
    add_member(db, tb, "b1", first_name="Henry", last_name="Miller", gender="m",
               date_of_birth="1920", additional_data="Note B", birthplace="Hamburg")

    preview = compute_merge_preview(db, user, ta.id, tb.id)

    assert preview.total_members == 2
    assert preview.merged_count == 1
    assert len(preview.duplicates) == 1
    pair = preview.duplicates[0]
    assert pair.match == "exact"
    assert pair.default_action == "merge"
    assert "additional_data" in pair.conflicts
    assert "birthplace" in pair.conflicts


def test_preview_possible_candidate(db):
    user = make_user(db, "alice")
    ta = make_tree(db, user, "A")
    tb = make_tree(db, user, "B")

    add_member(db, ta, "a1", first_name="Anna", last_name="Schmidt", gender="f",
               date_of_birth="1950")
    # Same name+gender but different birth date → possible
    add_member(db, tb, "b1", first_name="Anna", last_name="Schmidt", gender="f",
               date_of_birth="1951")

    preview = compute_merge_preview(db, user, ta.id, tb.id)

    assert preview.total_members == 2
    assert len(preview.duplicates) == 1
    pair = preview.duplicates[0]
    assert pair.match == "possible"

There's also `reconcile_bridge_fields` used by the tree-linking bridge-person flow, and `_clone_member`/`_wire_bridge` helpers. None of this writes in-place inside a single tree — it always clones into a new/different tree.

Goal: a guided IN-PLACE merge of two members of the SAME tree — pick a `keep_id` and a `remove_id`, resolve field conflicts, transfer all of remove's relations/content onto keep, then delete remove. Entry point launched from a `duplicate_candidate` finding in the quality report.

# Implementation Plan — Issue #729: In-place duplicate member merge

## Open design decisions (please sanity-check these first)

1. **Disease dedup policy** — I recommend **deduping** transferred `MemberDisease` rows by `(keep_id, normalized name)`, reusing the same `_norm(d.name)` policy the tree-merge already uses (`merge.py` lines 558–580). Rationale: after merging two records of the *same person*, two identical "Diabetes" rows are noise, and the tree-merge already set this precedent. Downside: you lose a differing `carrier_status`/`notes` on the dropped row. Alternative (keep both) is defensible since these are real content rows, not structural links — flagging so you can override.

2. **Bridge-link handling** — I recommend **carry-over-else-dissolve**: if `remove_id` is a bridge person and `keep_id` has no link of its own, re-point the bridge onto `keep_id` (rewire the counterpart back to `keep_id`); if `keep_id` already has its own link, dissolve `remove_id`'s bridge by clearing both sides of the counterpart (exactly like `delete_member` does at members.py:1157–1164). Alternative the issue floats — refuse the merge when both are separately linked — is stricter but more surprising to the user. Flagging.

3. **Picker-of-2 UI** — For a `duplicate_candidate` finding with N ids: if **N == 2**, open the dialog directly with keep=first / remove=second plus a "Swap" control; if **N > 2**, show two dropdowns inside the dialog (choose primary and duplicate, constrained distinct), defaulting to the first two. Simple, single dialog, no separate picker screen.

4. **Undo mechanism** — Do **not** reuse `useMemberStore`'s delete-with-grace-period undo. The merge action lives in `useQualityReportStore` and just refreshes report + members. Reversibility is served only by a rich activity-log pre-image payload (per #572), not a client-side undo. No layout re-run (see §Frontend/layout).

5. **`conflicts` field casing (important, load-bearing)** — The existing tree-merge `DuplicatePair.conflicts` are **snake_case** (`compute_conflicts` returns `CONFLICT_FIELDS`), but the frontend `RESOLVABLE_FIELDS` are **camelCase**, so `isFieldConflicting` in `MergeConflictResolver` silently fails to highlight/enable the Select for any multi-word field (`middleNames`, `additionalData`, `dateOfBirth`, …). To make the resolver fully functional in the new flow, my **preview endpoint returns `conflicts` as camelCase**, and my **merge endpoint normalizes incoming field keys camel→snake** (via `_to_snake_case`, already used by `reconcile_bridge_fields`) before calling `apply_field_choices`. I'm flagging the pre-existing tree-merge discrepancy but not fixing it here.

6. **Activity entry shape** — recorded as `action="update"`, `target_type="member"`, `target_id=keep_id`, with everything in `details["merge"]`. This renders as an ordinary member update in the existing activity UI while carrying a full pre-image for a future undo. (If you'd rather it read as a delete of `remove_id`, that's a one-line change.)

---

## Backend

### 1. `backend/app/services/quality_checks.py` — extract the cycle helper (modify)

Currently the cycle DFS is inline in `run_quality_checks` (section 3, lines 146–182). Extract it so both the report and the merge guard call one implementation:

```python
def find_parent_cycle_members(
    members: list[Member], relations: list[Relation]
) -> set[str]:
    """Return the set of member ids participating in a parent-chain cycle
    (empty when acyclic). Parent edge: relation_type=="parent",
    from_member_id=child, to_member_id=parent."""
```

Move the `parent_pairs` / `parents_of` / `_dfs` / `cycle_members` block into it. `run_quality_checks` calls it and keeps its existing issue-append. `parent_pairs` is still needed earlier in `run_quality_checks` for the age-gap checks, so leave that construction where it is and have the helper rebuild `parents_of` from the relations it receives (cheap, keeps the helper standalone).

### 2. `backend/app/schemas/merge.py` — new same-tree schemas (modify)

`DuplicatePair` fits the pair itself (reuse as-is; set `member_a`=keep, `member_b`=remove, `match` from `member_key` equality, `default_action="merge"`). Add:

```python
class MemberMergeTransferCounts(BaseModel):
    relations: int
    events: int
    stories: int
    gallery: int
    documents: int
    tasks: int
    diseases: int

class MemberMergePreviewOut(BaseModel):
    pair: DuplicatePair
    transfer: MemberMergeTransferCounts

class MemberMergeRequest(BaseModel):
    keep_id: str
    remove_id: str
    fields: dict[str, Literal["a", "b", "combine"]] = {}
```

These belong in `merge.py` (not `family.py`) since they reuse `DuplicatePair`/`MemberOut` and sit next to the other merge schemas.

### 3. `backend/app/services/member_merge.py` — new service module

Keep `merge.py` tree-focused; put the in-place logic here, importing the reusable pieces (`compute_conflicts`, `apply_field_choices`, `CONFLICT_FIELDS`, `_to_snake_case`, `_norm`, `member_key`) from `merge.py`.

**`compute_member_merge_preview(db, tree, keep_id, remove_id) -> MemberMergePreviewOut`**
- `keep = _get_member(...)`, `remove = _get_member(...)` (both must be in `tree`, else the route 404s — reuse the route's `_get_member`).
- `conflicts_snake = compute_conflicts(keep, remove)`; convert each to camelCase (`from pydantic.alias_generators import to_camel`) for the response.
- `match = "exact" if member_key(keep) == member_key(remove) else "possible"`.
- Build `DuplicatePair(member_a=MemberOut.model_validate(keep), member_b=MemberOut.model_validate(remove), match=match, conflicts=<camel list>, default_action="merge")`.
- Transfer counts — one `select(func.count())` per table filtered on `remove_id` (relations: `or_(from==remove, to==remove)`; the 5 link tables + `MemberDisease` on `member_id==remove`; gallery counts `GalleryMemberLink`).

**`merge_members_in_place(db, tree, user, keep_id, remove_id, fields) -> Member`** — everything below in one transaction (no `db.commit()` inside; the route commits):

1. **Guards** (the route already resolved `keep`/`remove` via `_get_member`, so 404 is handled there): if `keep_id == remove_id` → `HTTPException(400)`.
2. **Cycle guard** (before any mutation): load all `Relation` rows for `tree`, simulate the repoint in memory — for each parent relation replace `remove_id`→`keep_id` in both endpoints, drop self-edges — build the post-merge relation list, then call `find_parent_cycle_members(members_without_remove, simulated_relations)`. If non-empty → `HTTPException(400, "merge_creates_cycle")`. This catches the cases the issue calls out: `remove` is an ancestor of `keep` on another path, or they're each other's parents through different children — both collapse to a self/loop once `remove`'s edges fold onto `keep`.
3. **Activity pre-image** (capture BEFORE mutating): 
   - `removed_snapshot = member_delete_snapshot(db, remove, counterpart)["snapshot"]` (full pre-image of `remove` + its relations/diseases/5 link tables + optional bridge). Must run before repointing, since it reads rows still pointing at `remove_id`.
   - `keep_before = {f: getattr(keep, f) for f in CONFLICT_FIELDS}` (pre-overwrite copy of the fields resolution may change).
4. **Apply field choices onto keep**: normalize keys `normalized = {_to_snake_case(k): v for k, v in fields.items()}`, filter to `CONFLICT_FIELDS`, then `apply_field_choices(keep, keep, remove, normalized)`. Passing `clone=keep, ma=keep, mb=remove` makes `"a"` a no-op, `"b"` copy remove's value, `"combine"` union both (text fields only). No media copy needed — both members are in the same tree, so `image_data` URLs are already tree-local. `image_data` "combine" is silently ignored by `apply_field_choices` (not in its `text_fields`) — the UI won't offer it (`COMBINABLE_FIELDS` excludes `imageData`).
5. **Relations re-point** (composite PK `(tree_id, from, to, type)` — mutate-PK is risky, so delete-then-add):
   ```
   keep_keys = {(r.from, r.to, r.type) for r in relations if keep in (r.from, r.to)}
   new_rows = []
   for r in relations if remove in (r.from, r.to):
       nf = keep if r.from==remove else r.from
       nt = keep if r.to==remove else r.to
       db.delete(r)
       if nf == nt:              continue    # self-relation → drop
       key = (nf, nt, r.type)
       if key in keep_keys:      continue    # would duplicate a keep row → drop
       keep_keys.add(key); new_rows.append((nf, nt, r.type))
   db.flush()                                # deletes land before inserts
   for nf, nt, rt in new_rows:
       db.add(Relation(tree_id=tree.id, from_member_id=nf, to_member_id=nt, relation_type=rt))
   ```
6. **Content link tables** — `EventMemberLink`(event_id), `StoryMemberLink`(story_id), `GalleryMemberLink`(gallery_image_id), `DocumentMemberLink`(document_id), `MemberTaskLink`(task_id). All composite PK `(content_id, member_id)`; same delete-then-add drop-on-duplicate pattern:
   ```
   keep_content_ids = {link.<cid> for link in model if member_id==keep}
   for link in model if member_id==remove:
       if link.<cid> in keep_content_ids:  db.delete(link)        # dup → drop
       else:  db.delete(link); stage add(model(<cid>=..., member_id=keep, +extra cols))
   ```
   `GalleryMemberLink` carries `x/y/w/h` — preserve them on the re-added row (note: on a dup drop, `remove`'s face-region tag is lost in favor of `keep`'s existing link; acceptable).
7. **`MemberDisease`** (own `id` PK, `member_id` is a plain FK — safe to mutate): dedupe by `(keep_id, _norm(name))` against keep's existing diseases; repoint `member_id=keep_id` on survivors, `db.delete` the duplicates.

# Implementation Plan — Issue #729: In-place duplicate member merge

## Open design decisions (please sanity-check these first)

1. **Disease dedup policy** — I recommend **deduping** transferred `MemberDisease` rows by `(keep_id, normalized name)`, reusing the same `_norm(d.name)` policy the tree-merge already uses (`merge.py` lines 558–580). Rationale: after merging two records of the *same person*, two identical "Diabetes" rows are noise, and the tree-merge already set this precedent. Downside: you lose a differing `carrier_status`/`notes` on the dropped row. Alternative (keep both) is defensible since these are real content rows, not structural links — flagging so you can override.

2. **Bridge-link handling** — I recommend **carry-over-else-dissolve**: if `remove_id` is a bridge person and `keep_id` has no link of its own, re-point the bridge onto `keep_id` (rewire the counterpart back to `keep_id`); if `keep_id` already has its own link, dissolve `remove_id`'s bridge by clearing both sides of the counterpart (exactly like `delete_member` does at members.py:1157–1164). Alternative the issue floats — refuse the merge when both are separately linked — is stricter but more surprising to the user. Flagging.

3. **Picker-of-2 UI** — For a `duplicate_candidate` finding with N ids: if **N == 2**, open the dialog directly with keep=first / remove=second plus a "Swap" control; if **N > 2**, show two dropdowns inside the dialog (choose primary and duplicate, constrained distinct), defaulting to the first two. Simple, single dialog, no separate picker screen.

4. **Undo mechanism** — Do **not** reuse `useMemberStore`'s delete-with-grace-period undo. The merge action lives in `useQualityReportStore` and just refreshes report + members. Reversibility is served only by a rich activity-log pre-image payload (per #572), not a client-side undo. No layout re-run (see §Frontend/layout).

5. **`conflicts` field casing (important, load-bearing)** — The existing tree-merge `DuplicatePair.conflicts` are **snake_case** (`compute_conflicts` returns `CONFLICT_FIELDS`), but the frontend `RESOLVABLE_FIELDS` are **camelCase**, so `isFieldConflicting` in `MergeConflictResolver` silently fails to highlight/enable the Select for any multi-word field (`middleNames`, `additionalData`, `dateOfBirth`, …). To make the resolver fully functional in the new flow, my **preview endpoint returns `conflicts` as camelCase**, and my **merge endpoint normalizes incoming field keys camel→snake** (via `_to_snake_case`, already used by `reconcile_bridge_fields`) before calling `apply_field_choices`. I'm flagging the pre-existing tree-merge discrepancy but not fixing it here.

6. **Activity entry shape** — recorded as `action="update"`, `target_type="member"`, `target_id=keep_id`, with everything in `details["merge"]`. This renders as an ordinary member update in the existing activity UI while carrying a full pre-image for a future undo. (If you'd rather it read as a delete of `remove_id`, that's a one-line change.)

## Backend

### 1. `backend/app/services/quality_checks.py` — extract the cycle helper (modify)

Currently the cycle DFS is inline in `run_quality_checks` (section 3, lines 146–182). Extract it so both the report and the merge guard call one implementation:

```python
def find_parent_cycle_members(
    members: list[Member], relations: list[Relation]
) -> set[str]:
    """Return the set of member ids participating in a parent-chain cycle
    (empty when acyclic). Parent edge: relation_type=="parent",
    from_member_id=child, to_member_id=parent."""
```

Move the `parent_pairs` / `parents_of` / `_dfs` / `cycle_members` block into it. `run_quality_checks` calls it and keeps its existing issue-append. `parent_pairs` is still needed earlier in `run_quality_checks` for the age-gap checks, so leave that construction where it is and have the helper rebuild `parents_of` from the relations it receives (cheap, keeps the helper standalone).

### 2. `backend/app/schemas/merge.py` — new same-tree schemas (modify)

`DuplicatePair` fits the pair itself (reuse as-is; set `member_a`=keep, `member_b`=remove, `match` from `member_key` equality, `default_action="merge"`). Add:

```python
class MemberMergeTransferCounts(BaseModel):
    relations: int
    events: int
    stories: int
    gallery: int
    documents: int
    tasks: int

class MemberMergePreviewOut(BaseModel):

class MemberMergeRequest(BaseModel):
```

These belong in `merge.py` (not `family.py`) since they reuse `DuplicatePair`/`MemberOut` and sit next to the other merge schemas.

### 3. `backend/app/services/member_merge.py` — new service module

Keep `merge.py` tree-focused; put the in-place logic here, importing the reusable pieces (`compute_conflicts`, `apply_field_choices`, `CONFLICT_FIELDS`, `_to_snake_case`, `_norm`, `member_key`) from `merge.py`.

**`compute_member_merge_preview(db, tree, keep_id, remove_id) -> MemberMergePreviewOut`**
- `keep = _get_member(...)`, `remove = _get_member(...)` (both must be in `tree`, else the route 404s — reuse the route's `_get_member`).
- `conflicts_snake = compute_conflicts(keep, remove)`; convert each to camelCase (`from pydantic.alias_generators import to_camel`) for the response.
- `match = "exact" if member_key(keep) == member_key(remove) else "possible"`.
- Build `DuplicatePair(member_a=MemberOut.model_validate(keep), member_b=MemberOut.model_validate(remove), match=match, conflicts=<camel list>, default_action="merge")`.
- Transfer counts — one `select(func.count())` per table filtered on `remove_id` (relations: `or_(from==remove, to==remove)`; the 5 link tables + `MemberDisease` on `member_id==remove`; gallery counts `GalleryMemberLink`).

**`merge_members_in_place(db, tree, user, keep_id, remove_id, fields) -> Member`** — everything below in one transaction (no `db.commit()` inside; the route commits):

1. **Guards** (the route already resolved `keep`/`remove` via `_get_member`, so 404 is handled there): if `keep_id == remove_id` → `HTTPException(400)`.
2. **Cycle guard** (before any mutation): load all `Relation` rows for `tree`, simulate the repoint in memory — for each parent relation replace `remove_id`→`keep_id` in both endpoints, drop self-edges — build the post-merge relation list, then call `find_parent_cycle_members(members_without_remove, simulated_relations)`. If non-empty → `HTTPException(400, "merge_creates_cycle")`. This catches the cases the issue calls out: `remove` is an ancestor of `keep` on another path, or they're each other's parents through different children — both collapse to a self/loop once `remove`'s edges fold onto `keep`.
3. **Activity pre-image** (capture BEFORE mutating): 
   - `removed_snapshot = member_delete_snapshot(db, remove, counterpart)["snapshot"]` (full pre-image of `remove` + its relations/diseases/5 link tables + optional bridge). Must run before repointing, since it reads rows still pointing at `remove_id`.
   - `keep_before = {f: getattr(keep, f) for f in CONFLICT_FIELDS}` (pre-overwrite copy of the fields resolution may change).
4. **Apply field choices onto keep**: normalize keys `normalized = {_to_snake_case(k): v for k, v in fields.items()}`, filter to `CONFLICT_FIELDS`, then `apply_field_choices(keep, keep, remove, normalized)`. Passing `clone=keep, ma=keep, mb=remove` makes `"a"` a no-op, `"b"` copy remove's value, `"combine"` union both (text fields only). No media copy needed — both members are in the same tree, so `image_data` URLs are already tree-local. `image_data` "combine" is silently ignored by `apply_field_choices` (not in its `text_fields`) — the UI won't offer it (`COMBINABLE_FIELDS` excludes `imageData`).
5. **Relations re-point** (composite PK `(tree_id, from, to, type)` — mutate-PK is risky, so delete-then-add):
   ```
   keep_keys = {(r.from, r.to, r.type) for r in relations if keep in (r.from, r.to)}
   new_rows = []
   for r in relations if remove in (r.from, r.to):
       nf = keep if r.from==remove else r.from
       nt = keep if r.to==remove else r.to
       db.delete(r)
       if nf == nt:              continue    # self-relation → drop
       key = (nf, nt, r.type)
       if key in keep_keys:      continue    # would duplicate a keep row → drop
       keep_keys.add(key); new_rows.append((nf, nt, r.type))
   db.flush()                                # deletes land before inserts
   for nf, nt, rt in new_rows:
       db.add(Relation(tree_id=tree.id, from_member_id=nf, to_member_id=nt, relation_type=rt))
   ```
6. **Content link tables** — `EventMemberLink`(event_id), `StoryMemberLink`(story_id), `GalleryMemberLink`(gallery_image_id), `DocumentMemberLink`(document_id), `MemberTaskLink`(task_id). All composite PK `(content_id, member_id)`; same delete-then-add drop-on-duplicate pattern:
   ```
   keep_content_ids = {link.<cid> for link in model if member_id==keep}
   for link in model if member_id==remove:
       if link.<cid> in keep_content_ids:  db.delete(link)        # dup → drop
       else:  db.delete(link); stage add(model(<cid>=..., member_id=keep, +extra cols))
   ```
   `GalleryMemberLink` carries `x/y/w/h` — preserve them on the re-added row (note: on a dup drop, `remove`'s face-region tag is lost in favor of `keep`'s existing link; acceptable).
7. **`MemberDisease`** (own `id` PK, `member_id` is a plain FK — safe to mutate): dedupe by `(keep_id, _norm(name))` against keep's existing diseases; repoint `member_id=keep_id` on survivors, `db.delete` the duplicates.
8. **Bridge** (decision #2): if `remove.linked_member_id`: fetch counterpart; if `keep` unlinked → set `keep.linked_tree_id/linked_member_id` from remove and rewire `counterpart.linked_member_id=keep.id`, `counterpart.linked_tree_id=keep.tree_id`; else clear both counterpart pointers. Record `counterpart_tree` for side-effects. `GalleryUnknownFace` has no `member_id` — skip (confirmed in `content.py`).
9. **Delete** `remove` (`db.delete(remove)`). Everything member-scoped was re-pointed first, so the `CASCADE` on `member_id` only removes rows we already handled.
10. Build and return the `details` dict for the route to pass to `record_activity`:
    ```python
    details = {"merge": {
        "version": SNAPSHOT_VERSION,  # imported from activity.py
        "keep_id": keep.id,
        "removed": removed_snapshot,        # full pre-image of the deleted member
        "keep_before": keep_before,         # kept member's fields before resolution
        "field_choices": normalized,
    }}
    ```
    Return `(keep, details, counterpart_tree)` so the route records activity + fires side-effects.

### 4. `backend/app/api/routes/members.py` — two new routes (modify)

Both live here (the issue's preferred home; uses `get_writable_tree`). **Declare them before `/members/{member_id}`** so the literal `merge`/`merge-preview` segments aren't captured as member ids — note `merge-preview` is under `/members/{member_id}/…` so ordering vs the `{member_id}` GET matters; put the POST `/members/merge` alongside `positions`/`collapsed` (above `{member_id}`), and the preview under `{member_id}/merge-preview` after the `{member_id}` routes is fine since the path is more specific.

```python
@router.get("/members/{member_id}/merge-preview", response_model=MemberMergePreviewOut)
def get_member_merge_preview(member_id, other: str = Query(...), tree=Depends(get_writable_tree), user=..., db=...):
    keep = _get_member(db, tree, member_id)
    remove = _get_member(db, tree, other)          # 404 if not in this tree
    if keep.id == remove.id: raise HTTPException(400, ...)
    return compute_member_merge_preview(db, tree, member_id, other)

@router.post("/members/merge", response_model=MemberOut)
def merge_members(payload: MemberMergeRequest, tree=Depends(get_writable_tree), user=..., db=...):
    keep = _get_member(db, tree, payload.keep_id)
    remove = _get_member(db, tree, payload.remove_id)
    merged, details, counterpart_tree = merge_members_in_place(db, tree, user, payload.keep_id, payload.remove_id, payload.fields)
    record_activity(db, tree_id=tree.id, actor=user, action="update", target_type="member",
                    target_id=merged.id, target_label=<name>, details=details)
    db.commit()
    publish_tree_event(db, tree, "activity.entry_added", {"tree_id": tree.id})
    db.refresh(merged)
    publish_tree_event(db, tree, "tree.content_changed", {"tree_id": tree.id, "domain": "member"})
    invalidate_stats(tree.id)
    if counterpart_tree is not None:
        publish_tree_event(db, counterpart_tree, "tree.content_changed", {"tree_id": counterpart_tree.id, "domain": "member"})
        invalidate_stats(counterpart_tree.id)
    return merged
```

This mirrors `delete_member`'s side-effect set exactly (member domain only — same precedent as delete even though content links moved). Add imports for the new schemas/service.

### 5. Backend tests — `backend/tests/test_member_merge.py` (new)

Service-level (using `db`, `make_user`, `make_tree`, `add_member`, `share`) plus a few route-level (`client`, `auth`):

- **Relation re-point, happy path**: keep+remove share a child; after merge the child's parent relation points at keep.
- **Relation dedup (the integrity case)**: both keep and remove are parents of the same child (two rows). After merge only one `(child, keep, "parent")` survives — assert **no IntegrityError** and exactly one row.
- **Self-relation drop**: keep is remove's parent; after merge the `(keep, keep, "parent")` self-edge is dropped.
- **Link transfer, per table** (one test each or parametrized): create an `EventMemberLink`/`StoryMemberLink`/`GalleryMemberLink`/`DocumentMemberLink`/`MemberTaskLink`/`MemberDisease` on remove → assert it now belongs to keep. Include a dup case (link exists on both) → one row survives.
- **Guards**: `keep_id == remove_id` → 400; `remove_id` in a different tree → 404; cycle creation (remove is ancestor of keep on a separate path) → 400.
- **Field resolution**: `fields={"dateOfBirth": "b"}` (camelCase in) → keep adopts remove's DOB; `{"additionalData": "combine"}` → both notes present.
- **Activity payload shape**: after merge, the newest `ActivityLog` row has `json.loads(details)["merge"]` with `keep_id`, `removed.member`, `removed.relations`, `keep_before`, `field_choices`, `version`.
- **Preview endpoint**: conflicts returned in **camelCase**, `match`/`default_action` correct, transfer counts correct.
- **Bridge carry-over**: remove is a bridge person, keep unlinked → keep inherits link and counterpart re-points to keep.

### 7. Layout recompute
No manual positions. `mergeMembers` calls `refreshMembers`, which reloads persisted positions (dagre-computed on prior layouts) and re-derives edges in the worker; the kept node stays put and the removed node disappears. def issue_id_for(issue_type: str, member_ids: list[str]) -> str:
    """Deterministic id for an issue, derived from its type and members.

    Issues are recomputed fresh on every request rather than stored, so this
    id is what lets a dismissal survive across requests: as long as the same
    underlying data produces the same issue, it hashes to the same id.
    """
    key = f"{issue_type}|{','.join(sorted(member_ids))}"
    return hashlib.sha256(key.encode()).hexdigest()[:32]

"""In-place, same-tree member merge (#729).

Unlike ``app.services.merge`` (which clones two whole *trees* into a brand
new third tree), this combines two *members of the same tree*: one survives
(``keep``), the other is removed (``remove``) after everything it owns —
relations, content links, diseases, and an optional tree-in-tree bridge — has
been re-pointed onto ``keep``. Field-conflict detection/resolution is reused
from ``app.services.merge`` rather than forked.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from types import SimpleNamespace

from fastapi import HTTPException
from pydantic.alias_generators import to_camel
from sqlalchemy import func, or_, select
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

from app.models import (
    DocumentMemberLink,
    EventMemberLink,
    GalleryMemberLink,
    Member,
    MemberDisease,
    MemberTaskLink,
    Relation,
    StoryMemberLink,
    Tree,
    User,
)
from app.schemas.family import MemberOut
from app.schemas.merge import (
    DuplicatePair,
    MemberMergePreviewOut,
    MemberMergeTransferCounts,
)
from app.services.activity import SNAPSHOT_VERSION, member_delete_snapshot
from app.services.merge import (
    CONFLICT_FIELDS,
    _norm,
    _to_snake_case,
    apply_field_choices,
    compute_conflicts,
    member_key,
)
from app.services.quality_checks import find_parent_cycle_members


def compute_member_merge_preview(
    db: Session, tree: Tree, keep: Member, remove: Member
) -> MemberMergePreviewOut:
    """Field conflicts plus counts of what a merge would transfer onto ``keep``.

    Conflicts are reported in camelCase (unlike the tree-merge preview, whose
    ``conflicts`` are the raw snake_case attribute names) so the response
    lines up with the frontend's ``RESOLVABLE_FIELDS``/``MergeConflictResolver``
    without a translation layer on the client.
    """
    conflicts = [to_camel(field) for field in compute_conflicts(keep, remove)]
    match = "exact" if member_key(keep) == member_key(remove) else "possible"
    pair = DuplicatePair(
        member_a=MemberOut.model_validate(keep),
        member_b=MemberOut.model_validate(remove),
        match=match,
        conflicts=conflicts,
        default_action="merge",
    )

    def _count(model: type, column) -> int:
        return db.scalar(select(func.count()).where(column == remove.id)) or 0

    relations = (
        db.scalar(
            select(func.count())
            .select_from(Relation)
            .where(
                Relation.tree_id == tree.id,
                or_(
                    Relation.from_member_id == remove.id,
                    Relation.to_member_id == remove.id,
                ),
            )
        )
        or 0
    )

    transfer = MemberMergeTransferCounts(
        relations=relations,
        events=_count(EventMemberLink, EventMemberLink.member_id),
        stories=_count(StoryMemberLink, StoryMemberLink.member_id),
        gallery=_count(GalleryMemberLink, GalleryMemberLink.member_id),
        documents=_count(DocumentMemberLink, DocumentMemberLink.member_id),
        tasks=_count(MemberTaskLink, MemberTaskLink.member_id),
        diseases=_count(MemberDisease, MemberDisease.member_id),
    )
    return MemberMergePreviewOut(pair=pair, transfer=transfer)


def _repoint_member_links(
    db: Session,
    model: type,
    id_field: str,
    keep_id: str,
    remove_id: str,
    extra_fields: tuple[str, ...] = (),
) -> None:
    """Union a member-link table onto ``keep_id``, dropping duplicates.

    Every content link table (events, stories, gallery, documents, tasks) has
    the same composite-PK shape: ``(<content>_id, member_id)``. A link already
    on ``keep_id`` wins; ``remove_id``'s copy is simply dropped rather than
    causing a primary-key clash.
    """
    keep_ids = {
        getattr(row, id_field)
        for row in db.scalars(select(model).where(model.member_id == keep_id))
    }
    to_add: list[dict] = []
    for row in db.scalars(select(model).where(model.member_id == remove_id)):
        content_id = getattr(row, id_field)
        extras = {field: getattr(row, field) for field in extra_fields}
        db.delete(row)
        if content_id in keep_ids:
            continue
        keep_ids.add(content_id)
        to_add.append({id_field: content_id, "member_id": keep_id, **extras})
    db.flush()
    for kwargs in to_add:
        db.add(model(**kwargs))


def _transfer_diseases(db: Session, keep_id: str, remove_id: str) -> None:
    """Move ``remove``'s disease records onto ``keep``, deduping by name.

    Mirrors the tree-merge dedup policy (``app.services.merge``, diseases
    section): two rows naming the same condition on the same person are
    noise once the two records describe one person, so the duplicate is
    dropped rather than kept alongside.
    """
    keep_names = {
        _norm(d.name)
        for d in db.scalars(
            select(MemberDisease).where(MemberDisease.member_id == keep_id)
        )
    }
    for disease in db.scalars(
        select(MemberDisease).where(MemberDisease.member_id == remove_id)
    ):
        name_key = _norm(disease.name)
        if name_key in keep_names:
            db.delete(disease)

    db: Session, tree: Tree, keep: Member, remove: Member

    without a translation layer on the client.

    conflicts = [to_camel(field) for field in compute_conflicts(keep, remove)]
    match = "exact" if member_key(keep) == member_key(remove) else "possible"
    pair = DuplicatePair(
        member_a=MemberOut.model_validate(keep),
        member_b=MemberOut.model_validate(remove),

        default_action="merge",

    def _count(model: type, column) -> int:
        return db.scalar(select(func.count()).where(column == remove.id)) or 0

def _repoint_member_links(
    db: Session,

    keep_id: str,
    remove_id: str,

    causing a primary-key clash.

    keep_ids = {
        getattr(row, id_field)

        content_id = getattr(row, id_field)

"""Tests for the in-place, same-tree member merge (#729)."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json

from sqlalchemy import select

from app.models import (
    DocumentMemberLink,
    EventMemberLink,
    GalleryMemberLink,
    Member,
    MemberDisease,
    MemberTaskLink,
    Relation,
    StoryMemberLink,
)
from app.models.activity import ActivityLog
from app.models.content import (
    Document,
    Event,
    GalleryImage,
    MemberTask,
    Story,
)
from app.services.member_merge import (
    compute_member_merge_preview,
    merge_members_in_place,
)
from tests.conftest import API, add_member, make_tree, make_user, share

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Preview
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_preview_reports_camel_case_conflicts_and_transfer_counts(db):
    user = make_user(db, "alice")
    tree = make_tree(db, user, "T")
    keep = add_member(
        db, tree, "keep", first_name="Henry", last_name="Miller", gender="m",
        date_of_birth="1920", additional_data="Note A", birthplace="Berlin",
    )
    remove = add_member(
        db, tree, "remove", first_name="Henry", last_name="Miller", gender="m",
        date_of_birth="1920", additional_data="Note B", birthplace="Hamburg",
    )
    db.add(Relation(tree_id=tree.id, from_member_id="child", to_member_id="remove",
                     relation_type="parent"))
    add_member(db, tree, "child", first_name="Child", last_name="Miller")
    db.commit()

    preview = compute_member_merge_preview(db, tree, keep, remove)

    assert preview.pair.match == "exact"
    assert "additionalData" in preview.pair.conflicts
    assert "birthplace" in preview.pair.conflicts
    # snake_case names must not leak through
    assert "additional_data" not in preview.pair.conflicts
    assert preview.transfer.relations == 1


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Guard rails
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_self_merge_rejected(db):
    user = make_user(db, "alice")
    tree = make_tree(db, user, "T")
    keep = add_member(db, tree, "keep", first_name="A")

    from fastapi import HTTPException
    import pytest

    with pytest.raises(HTTPException) as exc:
        merge_members_in_place(db, tree, keep, keep, {})
    assert exc.value.status_code == 400


def test_route_rejects_cross_tree_members(db):
    user = make_user(db, "alice")
    tree_a = make_tree(db, user, "A")
    tree_b = make_tree(db, user, "B")
    add_member(db, tree_a, "keep", first_name="A")
    add_member(db, tree_b, "remove", first_name="B")

    from app.db.session import get_db
    from fastapi import FastAPI
    from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

    from app.api.router import api_router
    from app.core.config import settings as app_settings

    app = FastAPI()
    app.include_router(api_router, prefix=app_settings.API_PREFIX)

    def override_get_db():
        yield db

    app.dependency_overrides[get_db] = override_get_db
    client = TestClient(app)

    from tests.conftest import auth

    resp = client.post(
        f"{API}/trees/{tree_a.id}/members/merge",
        json={"keep_id": "keep", "remove_id": "remove", "fields": {}},
        headers=auth(user),
    )
    assert resp.status_code == 404


def test_merge_creates_cycle_is_rejected(db):
    user = make_user(db, "alice")
    tree = make_tree(db, user, "T")
    # keep is remove's parent, and remove is keep's grandparent through a
    # third member — merging keep into remove would fold "keep is remove's
    # parent" and "remove is grandparent of keep" into a self-referencing
    # parent edge.
    keep = add_member(db, tree, "keep", first_name="Keep")
    remove = add_member(db, tree, "remove", first_name="Remove")
    mid = add_member(db, tree, "mid", first_name="Mid")
    db.add(Relation(tree_id=tree.id, from_member_id="remove", to_member_id="keep",
                     relation_type="parent"))
    db.add(Relation(tree_id=tree.id, from_member_id="mid", to_member_id="remove",
                     relation_type="parent"))
    db.add(Relation(tree_id=tree.id, from_member_id="keep", to_member_id="mid",
                     relation_type="parent"))
    db.commit()

    from fastapi import HTTPException
    import pytest

    with pytest.raises(HTTPException) as exc:
        merge_members_in_place(db, tree, keep, remove, {})
    assert exc.value.status_code == 400


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Relations
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_relation_repointed_onto_keep(db):
    user = make_user(db, "alice")
    tree = make_tree(db, user, "T")
    keep = add_member(db, tree, "keep", first_name="Keep")
    remove = add_member(db, tree, "remove", first_name="Remove")
    add_member(db, tree, "child", first_name="Child")
    db.add(Relation(tree_id=tree.id, from_member_id="child", to_member_id="remove",
                     relation_type="parent"))
    db.commit()

    merge_members_in_place(db, tree, keep, remove, {})
    db.commit()

    relations = db.scalars(select(Relation).where(Relation.tree_id == tree.id)).all()
    assert len(relations) == 1
    assert relations[0].from_member_id == "child"
    assert relations[0].to_member_id == "keep"


def test_duplicate_relation_is_dropped_not_an_integrity_error(db):
    user = make_user(db, "alice")
    tree = make_tree(db, user, "T")
    keep = add_member(db, tree, "keep", first_name="Keep")
    remove = add_member(db, tree, "remove", first_name="Remove")

# Changelog

All notable changes to this project are documented here. The format is based on
[Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/), and this project
adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

Releases are cut from `vX.Y.Z` Git tags; pushing a tag publishes the matching
Docker images to GHCR (see [docs/OPERATIONS.md](docs/OPERATIONS.md)).

## [Unreleased]

### Added

- A member's profile picture can now be set from one of their already-linked
  gallery photos (with crop), instead of only by uploading a new file (#776).
- Data-quality report now flags a child born after a parent's death year. A
  posthumous-birth grace window (~1 year) is allowed for fathers and
  parents of unknown gender, but not for mothers (#768).
- Data-quality report now flags a life event dated after the linked member's
  own death year (a new `event_after_death` warning). Burial events are
  excluded, since they legitimately occur after death (#799).
- Research tasks: open questions and to-dos with open/done state, linked to
  any number of members (or none, for general tree-wide tasks), managed from
  the member sheet or created directly from the quality report. Tree nodes can
  show a toggleable indicator for members with open tasks, the quality report
  lists all open research items, and task changes appear in the activity log.
  Gated behind the new `research_tasks` feature flag (#725).
- Gallery face tags can now be marked as an "unknown person" (no member),
  which creates exactly one open, tree-level research task to identify them
  later. Resolving the tag to a member closes its task and turns the tag into
  a normal member link; deleting the tag removes its still-open task, while a
  completed task is kept as history. Gated behind the `research_tasks`
  feature flag (#736).
- Each Records section (Gallery, Events, Stories, Documents, Genetic
  Conditions, Research Tasks) in the member sheet can now be collapsed or
  expanded as a whole via its header, independent of the existing
  show-more/show-less within a section. Collapse state is remembered per
  section across reopening the sheet (#782).
- Gallery thumbnails now show the names of linked members below the title,

## Summary

Connects two previously-separate subsystems per #729: the quality report's
`duplicate_candidate` findings (which only offered *dismiss*) and the
tree-merge field-conflict machinery (`compute_merge_preview` /
`apply_field_choices` from #166), so a duplicate finding can now be resolved
with a guided **in-place** merge of two members of the same tree.

- **Backend**: `GET /trees/{id}/members/{id}/merge-preview` and
  `POST /trees/{id}/members/merge` (`keep_id`, `remove_id`, `fields`), backed
  by a new `member_merge` service that:
  - reuses `compute_conflicts` / `apply_field_choices` from the existing
    tree-merge service rather than forking the logic;
  - unions relations and content links (events, stories, gallery, documents,
    research tasks, diseases) onto the kept member, **deduping** instead of
    raising an integrity error when the union would produce a duplicate row,
    and dropping relations that become self-referencing once both ends fold
    onto the same member;
  - refuses to merge a member with itself, and refuses a merge that would
    create a relationship cycle — the cycle-detection DFS is extracted out of
    `quality_checks.run_quality_checks` into `find_parent_cycle_members` so
    the report and the merge guard agree on what counts as a cycle;
  - carries a tree-in-tree bridge link onto the kept member when only the
    removed member had one, otherwise dissolves it (mirroring the existing
    single-member-delete behavior);
  - records a rich `record_activity` payload (full pre-image of the removed
    member + its relations/links/diseases, plus the kept member's
    pre-resolution field values) so a future undo feature (#572) has enough
    to work with.
- **Frontend**: a "Merge…" action on `duplicate_candidate` findings in
  `QualityReportView` opens `MergeMembersDialog`, which reuses the existing
  `MergeConflictResolver` (already shared with the tree-in-tree linking flow)
  for side-by-side field resolution, shows a preview of what will transfer,
  and lets the user pick which two members to merge when a finding lists more
  than two same-named members.
- Entry point lives behind the existing `quality_report` feature flag (the
  quality report view is already gated); the merge/preview endpoints
  themselves are core member CRUD and are **not** separately flagged, per the
  issue's guidance.
- CHANGELOG entry added under `Unreleased`.

- [x] Backend: `uv run ruff check`, `uv run pytest -n auto` (full suite, incl.

message.content: what happens when a bridging person is merged with some other person? or if it were two bridging people

content.text:
Good question — the logic is deliberate but has one nuance worth being upfront about. Here's what actually happens, based on `merge_members_in_place` in `backend/app/services/member_merge.py`:

**Case 1: the removed member was the bridge person, the kept member wasn't**

The bridge is *carried over* onto the survivor:
- `keep` inherits `remove`'s `linked_tree_id`/`linked_member_id`.
- The counterpart row in the other tree gets re-pointed to `keep` instead of `remove`.
- A `tree.content_changed` event fires for that other tree so any open client refreshes and sees the bridge now pointing at `keep`.

This makes sense semantically: the two merged records were claimed to be the same person, so whichever one was bridging to another tree, that identity naturally continues via the survivor.

**Case 2: both the kept and removed members are (separately) bridge people**

A `Member` row can only hold *one* bridge link (`linked_tree_id`/`linked_member_id` is a single pair, not a list), so both links can't survive a merge into one row. My implementation keeps `keep`'s original bridge untouched and **dissolves** `remove`'s bridge — its counterpart gets `linked_tree_id`/`linked_member_id` set to `None` (becomes an ordinary, unlinked member in its own tree, not deleted). This exactly mirrors what already happens today when you plain-delete one half of a bridge pair (`delete_member` in `members.py`).

**Case 3 (theoretical): both point at the exact same counterpart**

Not reachable through the normal API — linking already enforces a strict 1:1 pairing (you can't link a member, or link *to* a member, that's already linked to something else), so two distinct members in one tree can't both be bridging to the same third member.

**One gap worth flagging**: in Case 1 (the "inherit" scenario), I only fire a `tree.content_changed` ping for the other tree — I don't write a second activity-log entry there, even though the counterpart's linked-member id materially changed. I matched `delete_member`'s precedent (which also only pings, never double-logs on dissolve), but that precedent is for a pure dissolve; `link_member_to_tree` — the closer analog for "a bridge now points somewhere new" — *does* write an activity entry on both sides. So someone reviewing the counterpart tree's activity log won't see any record explaining why their bridge partner's identity changed. I can add that second `record_activity` call if you'd like it fixed before merge — want me to?

    add_member(db, tree, "keep", first_name="Keep", last_name="Person")
    add_member(
        db, tree, "remove", first_name="Remove", last_name="Person",
        linked_tree_id=other.id, linked_member_id="counterpart",
    )
    add_member(
        db, other, "counterpart", first_name="Remove", last_name="Person",
        linked_tree_id=tree.id, linked_member_id="remove",
    )
    db.commit()

    resp = client.post(
        f"{API}/trees/{tree.id}/members/merge",
        json={"keep_id": "keep", "remove_id": "remove", "fields": {}},
        headers=auth(user),
    )
    assert resp.status_code == 200

    assert keep.linked_member_id == "counterpart"
    counterpart = db.get(Member, "counterpart")
    assert counterpart.linked_tree_id == tree.id

def test_field_choice_combine_unions_additional_data(db):
    user = make_user(db, "alice")
    tree = make_tree(db, user, "T")
    keep = add_member(db, tree, "keep", first_name="Keep", additional_data="Note A")
    remove = add_member(db, tree, "remove", first_name="Remove", additional_data="Note B")

    merge_members_in_place(db, tree, keep, remove, {"additionalData": "combine"})
    db.commit()

    assert "Note A" in keep.additional_data
    assert "Note B" in keep.additional_data


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Activity log
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_merge_route_records_rich_activity_payload(client, db):
    user = make_user(db, "alice")
    tree = make_tree(db, user, "T")
    add_member(db, tree, "keep", first_name="Keep", last_name="Person")
    add_member(db, tree, "remove", first_name="Remove", last_name="Person")

    resp = client.post(
        f"{API}/trees/{tree.id}/members/merge",
        json={"keep_id": "keep", "remove_id": "remove", "fields": {}},
        headers=auth(user),
    )
    assert resp.status_code == 200
    assert resp.json()["id"] == "keep"

    assert db.get(Member, "remove") is None

    row = db.scalars(
        select(ActivityLog)
        .where(ActivityLog.tree_id == tree.id)
        .order_by(ActivityLog.id.desc())
    ).first()
    details = json.loads(row.details)
    merge_details = details["merge"]
    assert merge_details["keep_id"] == "keep"
    assert merge_details["removed"]["member"]["id"] == "remove"
    assert "keep_before" in merge_details
    assert "field_choices" in merge_details


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Tree-in-tree bridge handling
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_bridge_link_inherited_onto_keep_and_logged_in_other_tree(client, db):
    user = make_user(db, "alice")
    tree = make_tree(db, user, "T")
    other = make_tree(db, user, "Other")
    add_member(db, tree, "keep", first_name="Keep", last_name="Person")
    add_member(
        db, tree, "remove", first_name="Remove", last_name="Person",
        linked_tree_id=other.id, linked_member_id="counterpart",
    )
    add_member(
        db, other, "counterpart", first_name="Remove", last_name="Person",
        linked_tree_id=tree.id, linked_member_id="remove",
    )
    db.commit()

    resp = client.post(
        f"{API}/trees/{tree.id}/members/merge",
        json={"keep_id": "keep", "remove_id": "remove", "fields": {}},
        headers=auth(user),
    )
    assert resp.status_code == 200

    keep = db.get(Member, "keep")
    assert keep.linked_tree_id == other.id
    assert keep.linked_member_id == "counterpart"
    counterpart = db.get(Member, "counterpart")
    assert counterpart.linked_tree_id == tree.id
    assert counterpart.linked_member_id == "keep"

    row = db.scalars(
        select(ActivityLog)
        .where(ActivityLog.tree_id == other.id)
        .order_by(ActivityLog.id.desc())
    ).first()
    assert row is not None
    assert row.target_id == "counterpart"
    bridge_details = json.loads(row.details)
    assert bridge_details["after"] == {
        "linked_tree_id": tree.id,
        "linked_member_id": "keep",
    }

def test_bridge_link_inherited_onto_keep_and_logged_in_other_tree(client, db):
    user = make_user(db, "alice")
    tree = make_tree(db, user, "T")
    other = make_tree(db, user, "Other")
    add_member(db, tree, "keep", first_name="Keep", last_name="Person")
    remove = add_member(db, tree, "remove", first_name="Remove", last_name="Person")
    counterpart = add_member(
        db, other, "counterpart", first_name="Remove", last_name="Person",
    )
    # Wire the bridge after both rows exist — linked_member_id is a real FK.
    remove.linked_tree_id = other.id
    remove.linked_member_id = "counterpart"
    counterpart.linked_tree_id = tree.id
    counterpart.linked_member_id = "remove"
    db.commit()

    resp = client.post(
        f"{API}/trees/{tree.id}/members/merge",
        json={"keep_id": "keep", "remove_id": "remove", "fields": {}},
        headers=auth(user),
    )
    assert resp.status_code == 200

    keep = db.get(Member, "keep")
    assert keep.linked_tree_id == other.id
    assert keep.linked_member_id == "counterpart"
    counterpart = db.get(Member, "counterpart")
    assert counterpart.linked_tree_id == tree.id
    assert counterpart.linked_member_id == "keep"

    row = db.scalars(
        select(ActivityLog)
        .where(ActivityLog.tree_id == other.id)
        .order_by(ActivityLog.id.desc())
    ).first()
    assert row is not None
    assert row.target_id == "counterpart"
    bridge_details = json.loads(row.details)
    assert bridge_details["after"] == {
        "linked_tree_id": tree.id,
        "linked_member_id": "keep",
    }

content.text:
Both fixes are pushed to PR #812. Summary:

1. **Bridge activity logging**: when a merge re-points or dissolves a tree-in-tree bridge link, the counterpart's tree now gets its own activity-log entry (previously only a live refresh event, no audit trail) — `merge_members_in_place` now returns the counterpart member + outcome (`"inherited"`/`"dissolved"`) so the route can record it, mirroring `link_member_to_tree`'s existing two-entry pattern. Added two new tests covering both outcomes and their logged payloads.

2. **"Keep both" toggle**: you were right that it made no sense — selecting it silently snapped back to "merge" with no visible effect. Added an opt-in `hideActionToggle` prop to `MergeConflictResolver` (default off, so the tree-merge and link-existing-tree dialogs are unaffected) and set it in `MergeMembersDialog`. Added a regression test asserting the toggle doesn't render there. (Note: `LinkExistingTreeDialog` has this exact same forced-override pattern already — same non-functional toggle — but I left it alone since it's out of scope here; flag if you'd like that fixed too.)

Full backend (`pytest -n auto`, 100%) and frontend (`vitest`, `tsc`, `check-i18n`) suites all green.
